title.zh: 卷一 本紀第一 武帝上
title.raw: 卷一 本紀第一 武帝上 Volume 1 Annals 1: Emperor Wu 1

sentences.zh: 初為冠軍孫無終司馬。

translations.literal: At first he served as Registrar under Champion-General Sun Wuzhong.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as registrar on the staff of Champion-General Sun Wuzhong.

sentences.zh: 安帝隆安三年十一月，妖賊孫恩作亂於會稽，晉朝衞將軍謝琰、前將軍劉牢之東討。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year of Long'an under Emperor An, the demonic rebel Sun En raised a revolt in Kuaiji; the Jin court's Defender-General Xie Yan and Forward-General Liu Laozhi marched east to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Emperor An's third Long'an year, the rebel leader Sun En rose in Kuaiji. The Jin Defender-General Xie Yan and Forward-General Liu Laozhi led an eastern campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 牢之請高祖參府軍事。

translations.literal: Laozhi requested that Gaozu join his headquarters as a staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi asked that Gaozu serve on his staff as a military aide.

sentences.zh: 十二月，牢之至吳，而賊緣道屯結，牢之命高祖與數十人覘賊遠近。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Laozhi reached Wu, but the bandits had massed along the route; Laozhi ordered Gaozu, with several dozen men, to scout how near the enemy lay.
translations.idiomatic: When Laozhi reached Wu in the twelfth month, rebels were encamped all along the road. He sent Gaozu with a few dozen men to reconnoiter the enemy's distance.

sentences.zh: 會遇賊至，眾數千人，高祖便進與戰。

translations.literal: They happened upon the rebels; the force numbered several thousand, and Gaozu at once advanced to give battle.
translations.idiomatic: They ran straight into the rebels—several thousand strong—and Gaozu charged straight into the fight.

sentences.zh: 所將人多死，而戰意方厲，手奮長刀，所殺傷甚眾。

translations.literal: Most of the men he led were killed, yet his fighting spirit only grew fiercer; wielding a long blade by hand, he killed and wounded a great many.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his men fell, but his ardor only sharpened. He swung a long saber himself and cut down a great number of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 牢之子敬宣疑高祖淹久，恐為賊所困，乃輕騎尋之。

translations.literal: Laozhi's son Jingxuan suspected that Gaozu had been delayed too long and feared he was trapped by the rebels, so he took a light cavalry detachment to search for him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan, Laozhi's son, feared Gaozu had been away too long and might be surrounded; he rode out with a small mounted party to find him.

sentences.zh: 既而眾騎並至，賊乃奔退，斬獲千餘人，推鋒而進，平山陰，恩遁還入海。

translations.literal: Before long the main cavalry arrived as well; the rebels then broke and fled. More than a thousand were killed or captured, and pressing the attack they advanced, pacified Shanyin, and En fled back to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rest of the cavalry came up, the rebels broke, and over a thousand were killed or taken. They drove forward, secured Shanyin, and En escaped back to sea.

sentences.zh: 四年五月，恩復入會稽，殺衞將軍謝琰。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year En again entered Kuaiji and killed Defender-General Xie Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the following year En re-entered Kuaiji and killed Xie Yan, the Defender-General.

sentences.zh: 十一月，劉牢之復率眾東征，恩退走。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Liu Laozhi again led his troops on an eastern campaign, and En withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: That November Laozhi marched east again, and En retreated.

sentences.zh: 牢之屯上虞，使高祖戍句章城。

translations.literal: Laozhi encamped at Shangyu and ordered Gaozu to garrison Gouzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi stationed his force at Shangyu and left Gaozu to hold Gouzhang city.

sentences.zh: 句章城既卑小，戰士不盈數百人，高祖常被堅執銳，為士卒先，每戰輒摧鋒陷陣，賊乃退還浹口。

translations.literal: Gouzhang was low and small, and the fighting men numbered no more than a few hundred; Gaozu often donned armor and took up sharp weapons, going before the soldiers, and in every battle he shattered the enemy vanguard and broke their lines, so that the rebels withdrew to Jiakou.
translations.idiomatic: The city was small and weak, with only a few hundred defenders. Gaozu repeatedly buckled on armor, seized the vanguard, and in every clash broke the enemy front, driving the rebels back to Jiakou.

sentences.zh: 于時東伐諸帥，御軍無律，士卒暴掠，甚為百姓所苦。

translations.literal: At that time the commanders on the eastern campaign had no discipline over their troops; the soldiers plundered violently and the people suffered greatly from them.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern commanders kept no order; their troops looted at will, and the populace suffered terribly.

sentences.zh: 唯高祖法令明整，所至莫不親賴焉。

translations.literal: Only under Gaozu were the laws and orders clear and strict; wherever he went none failed to trust and rely on him.
translations.idiomatic: Only Gaozu's camp was governed by clear, strict discipline, and wherever he went the people placed their trust in him.

sentences.zh: 五年春，孫恩頻攻句章，高祖屢摧破之，恩復走入海。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year Sun En repeatedly attacked Gouzhang; Gaozu defeated him time and again, and En again fled to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the fifth year En assaulted Gouzhang again and again; Gaozu repulsed him repeatedly until En once more fled to sea.

sentences.zh: 三月，恩北出海鹽，高祖追而翼之，築城于海鹽故治。

translations.literal: In the third month En came north out to sea from Haiyan; Gaozu pursued and took him on the flank, and built a fort at the old seat of Haiyan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month En moved north from the sea toward Haiyan. Gaozu pursued, outflanked him, and fortified the old Haiyan administrative seat.

sentences.zh: 賊日來攻城，城內兵力甚弱，高祖乃選敢死之士數百人，咸脫甲冑，執短兵，並鼓噪而出，賊震懼奪氣，因其懼而奔之，並棄甲散走，斬其大帥姚盛。

translations.literal: The rebels came daily to assault the city; the force within was very weak. Gaozu then selected several hundred daredevils, all stripped of armor, grasping short weapons; together they rushed out with war cries. The rebels were shaken and lost heart; taking advantage of their fear he pursued them, and they all cast off armor and scattered in flight; their great commander Yao Sheng was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels attacked every day, and the garrison was desperately weak. Gaozu picked several hundred volunteers, stripped them of armor, armed them with short weapons, and led them out in a roaring charge. The enemy panicked; he pressed the rout, they threw down their armor and fled, and he slew their commander Yao Sheng.

sentences.zh: 雖連戰剋勝，然眾寡不敵，高祖獨深慮之。

translations.literal: Though he won victory in battle after battle, his numbers could not match the enemy's, and Gaozu alone was deeply troubled.
translations.idiomatic: He won fight after fight, yet he was badly outnumbered, and Gaozu brooded over the odds alone.

sentences.zh: 一夜，偃旗匿眾，若已遁者。

translations.literal: One night he lowered the banners and hid his troops, as if he had already fled.
translations.idiomatic: One night he furled the banners and concealed his men, feigning evacuation.

sentences.zh: 明晨開門，使羸疾數人登城。

translations.literal: At dawn he opened the gates and had a few sickly men climb the wall.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak he opened the gates and posted a handful of weak, sickly men on the ramparts.

sentences.zh: 賊遙問劉裕所在。

translations.literal: From afar the rebels asked where Liu Yu was.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels shouted from a distance, asking where Liu Yu had gone.

sentences.zh: 曰：「夜已走矣。

translations.literal: They replied, "He fled in the night.
translations.idiomatic: The answer came: "He slipped away last night.

sentences.zh: 」賊信之，乃率眾大上。

translations.literal: " The rebels believed it and then led their masses up in force.
translations.idiomatic: " The enemy believed them and swarmed up to storm the walls.

sentences.zh: 高祖乘其懈怠，奮擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Gaozu, while they were slack, struck hard and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: When their guard dropped, Gaozu struck and smashed them completely.

sentences.zh: 恩知城不可下，乃進向滬瀆。

translations.literal: En saw the city could not be taken and then advanced toward Hudu.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the city would not fall, En marched on toward Hudu.

sentences.zh: 高祖復棄城追之。

translations.literal: Gaozu again abandoned the city to pursue him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu again abandoned the fort and gave chase.

sentences.zh: 海鹽令鮑陋遣子嗣之以吳兵一千，請為前驅。

translations.literal: Bao Lou, the magistrate of Haiyan, sent his son Sizhi with a thousand Wu troops to serve as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Lou, magistrate of Haiyan, offered his son Sizhi with a thousand Wu soldiers as the advance guard.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「賊兵甚精，吳人不習戰，若前驅失利，必敗我軍。

translations.literal: Gaozu said, "The rebel soldiers are very skilled; the men of Wu are not accustomed to fighting. If the vanguard is defeated, it will surely ruin our army.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "The rebels fight well, and Wu men are not used to war. If the van is broken, our whole force will be undone.

sentences.zh: 可在後為聲援。

translations.literal: They should follow in the rear as a supporting force.
translations.idiomatic: Let them come behind as a reserve.

sentences.zh: 」不從。

translations.literal: " They did not heed him.
translations.idiomatic: " His advice was ignored.

sentences.zh: 是夜，高祖多設伏兵，兼置旗鼓，然一處不過數人。

translations.literal: That night Gaozu set many ambushes and also planted banners and drums, yet at any one spot there were no more than a few men.
translations.idiomatic: That night he laid many ambushes and planted flags and drums, though no single post held more than a handful of men.

sentences.zh: 明日，賊率眾萬餘迎戰。

translations.literal: The next day the rebels led more than ten thousand men to meet battle.
translations.idiomatic: Next day the enemy brought more than ten thousand men to fight.

sentences.zh: 前驅既交，諸伏皆出，舉旗鳴鼓。

translations.literal: Once the vanguard had joined combat, all the ambushes came out, raising banners and beating drums.
translations.idiomatic: When the van clashed, every ambush rose at once, flags flying and drums thundering.

sentences.zh: 賊謂四面有軍，乃退。

translations.literal: The rebels thought armies were on every side and then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels imagined armies on all sides and fell back.

sentences.zh: 嗣之追奔，為賊所沒。

translations.literal: Sizhi pursued the fleeing enemy and was overwhelmed by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhi chased the retreat and was cut off and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 高祖且戰且退，賊盛，所領死傷且盡。

translations.literal: Gaozu fought as he withdrew; the rebels were strong, and those under his command were killed and wounded until almost none remained.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu fought a fighting retreat; the enemy pressed hard, and his men were killed or wounded until nearly none were left.

sentences.zh: 高祖慮不免，至向伏兵處，乃止，令左右脫取死人衣。

translations.literal: Gaozu feared he could not escape; when he reached the place of the ambush he halted and ordered his attendants to strip the dead of their garments.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing capture, he reached his ambush line, stopped, and told his men to strip clothing from the corpses.

sentences.zh: 賊謂當走反停，疑猶有伏。

translations.literal: The rebels thought that one who should have fled had instead halted, and suspected there were still ambushes.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy, expecting flight, were baffled by the halt and suspected another trap.

sentences.zh: 高祖因呼更戰，氣色甚猛，賊眾以為然，乃引軍去。

translations.literal: Gaozu then shouted for another round of fighting, his bearing very fierce; the rebel masses took it to be so and then led their army away.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu called for another charge, his manner ferocious; the rebels took him at his word and drew off.

sentences.zh: 高祖徐歸，然後散兵稍集。

translations.literal: Gaozu withdrew slowly, and only then did his scattered troops gradually reassemble.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew at an easy pace, and only then did his scattered soldiers straggle back.

sentences.zh: 五月，孫恩破滬瀆，殺吳國內史袁山松，死者四千人。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Sun En broke Hudu and killed Yuan Shansong, Interior Governor of Wu, and four thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month En overran Hudu and killed Yuan Shansong, governor of Wu commandery; four thousand perished.

sentences.zh: 是月，高祖復破賊於婁縣。

translations.literal: That month Gaozu again defeated the rebels at Lou County.
translations.idiomatic: The same month Gaozu beat the rebels again at Lou.

sentences.zh: 六月，恩乘勝浮海，奄至丹徒，戰士十餘萬。

translations.literal: In the sixth month En, riding his victory, put to sea and suddenly reached Dantu with more than a hundred thousand fighting men.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month En sailed from his victory straight to Dantu with an army of more than a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 劉牢之猶屯山陰，京邑震動。

translations.literal: Liu Laozhi was still encamped at Shanyin, and the capital region was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Laozhi remained at Shanyin, and panic spread through the capital.

sentences.zh: 高祖倍道兼行，與賊俱至。

translations.literal: Gaozu pressed on by forced marches day and night and arrived with the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu marched day and night and arrived with the enemy force.

sentences.zh: 于時眾力既寡，加以步遠疲勞，而丹徒守軍莫有鬭志。

translations.literal: At that time their strength was already scant, and in addition the infantry were worn from the long march; moreover the garrison at Dantu had no will to fight.
translations.idiomatic: His numbers were few, his foot soldiers exhausted from the rush, and the Dantu garrison had no stomach for battle.

sentences.zh: 恩率眾數萬，鼓噪登蒜山，居民皆荷擔而立。

translations.literal: En led tens of thousands of men, beating drums and shouting as they climbed Garlic Mountain; the inhabitants all stood with carrying-poles on their shoulders.
translations.idiomatic: En led tens of thousands up Garlic Mountain with drums and shouts; townspeople stood ready with bundles on their shoulders to flee.

sentences.zh: 高祖率所領奔擊，大破之，投巘赴水死者甚眾。

translations.literal: Gaozu led those under his command in a rush attack and routed them utterly; very many were killed casting themselves into gullies or drowning in the water.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu charged and broke them; vast numbers plunged into ravines or drowned.

sentences.zh: 恩以彭排

translations.literal: En used a pengpai
translations.idiomatic: En boarded a covered assault barge

sentences.zh: 〈音敗〉

translations.literal: 〈pronounced bai〉
translations.idiomatic: (pronounced bai)

sentences.zh: 自載，[2]僅得還船。

translations.literal: to carry himself and barely got back to his ship.
translations.idiomatic: and barely made it back to his ship.

sentences.zh: 雖被摧破，猶恃其眾力，徑向京師。

translations.literal: Though he had been shattered, he still relied on the strength of his masses and headed straight for the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Broken though he was, he still trusted his numbers and steered straight for the capital.

sentences.zh: 樓船高大，值風不得進，旬日乃至白石。

translations.literal: The tower ships were tall and large; meeting wind they could not advance, and only after ten days did they reach Baishi.
translations.idiomatic: His tall war-junks met contrary winds and could not advance; ten days passed before they reached Baishi.

sentences.zh: 尋知劉牢之已還，朝廷有備，遂走向鬱洲。

translations.literal: Soon he learned that Liu Laozhi had already returned and that the court was prepared, and he then turned toward Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Laozhi had returned and the court was ready, he turned toward Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 八月，以高祖為建武將軍、下邳太守，領水軍追討至鬱洲，[3]復大破恩。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Gaozu was made General Who Establishes Martial Might and Administrator of Xiapi, commanding the navy in pursuit to Yuzhou, and again routed En thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he was appointed General Who Establishes Martial Might and Administrator of Xiapi, led the fleet in pursuit to Yuzhou, and again crushed En.

sentences.zh: 恩南走。

translations.literal: En fled south.
translations.idiomatic: En fled southward.

sentences.zh: 十一月，高祖追恩於滬瀆，及海鹽，又破之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Gaozu pursued En at Hudu and at Haiyan and defeated him again.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he pursued En to Hudu and Haiyan and beat him again.

sentences.zh: 三戰並大獲，俘馘以萬數。

translations.literal: In three battles he won great spoils, and captives and severed heads numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Three great victories yielded tens of thousands of prisoners and heads.

sentences.zh: 恩自是饑饉疾疫，死者太半，自浹口奔臨海。

translations.literal: From then on En suffered famine and pestilence; more than half his men died, and he fled from Jiakou to Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: Famine and plague then ravaged En's host; more than half died, and he fled from Jiakou toward Linhai.

sentences.zh: 元興元年正月，驃騎將軍司馬元顯西伐荊州刺史桓玄，玄亦率荊楚大眾，下討元顯。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Yuanxing, General of Agile Cavalry Sima Yuanxian campaigned west against Jingzhou Inspector Huan Xuan; Xuan also led the great host of Jing and Chu downstream to attack Yuanxian.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Yuanxing 1, General of Agile Cavalry Sima Yuanxian marched west against Jingzhou inspector Huan Xuan; Xuan in turn led the armies of Jing and Chu downriver to attack him.

sentences.zh: 元顯遣鎮北將軍劉牢之拒之，高祖參其軍事。

translations.literal: Yuanxian sent the Pacifier of the North Liu Laozhi to oppose him; Gaozu served on his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanxian sent Pacifier of the North Liu Laozhi to block him, with Gaozu on his staff.

sentences.zh: 次溧洲。

translations.literal: They halted at Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: They encamped at Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 玄至，高祖請擊之，不許，將遣子敬宣詣玄請和。

translations.literal: When Xuan arrived, Gaozu requested to attack him but was not permitted; they were about to send the son Jingxuan to Xuan to sue for peace.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuan arrived, Gaozu urged an attack but was refused; Laozhi meant to send Jingxuan to negotiate peace.

sentences.zh: 高祖與牢之甥東海何無忌並固諫，不從。

translations.literal: Gaozu and Laozhi's nephew from Donghai, He Wuji, together remonstrated firmly, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu and Laozhi's nephew He Wuji of Donghai pleaded together, to no avail.

sentences.zh: [4]遂遣敬宣詣玄。

translations.literal: [4] They then sent Jingxuan to Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: [4] Jingxuan was duly sent to Xuan.

sentences.zh: 玄剋京邑，殺元顯，以牢之為會稽內史。

translations.literal: Xuan took the capital, killed Yuanxian, and made Laozhi Interior Governor of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan seized the capital, killed Yuanxian, and appointed Laozhi interior governor of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 懼而告高祖曰：「便奪我兵，禍其至矣。

translations.literal: In fear he told Gaozu, "He is about to take my troops from me; disaster is at hand.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Laozhi told Gaozu, "He will strip me of my army—that means my ruin.

sentences.zh: 今當北就高雅於廣陵舉事，卿能從我去乎？

translations.literal: Now I should go north to join Gao Ya at Guangling and raise a revolt; can you come away with me?
translations.idiomatic: I mean to go north to Gao Ya at Guangling and rise in arms. Will you come with me?

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「將軍以勁卒數萬，望風降服。

translations.literal: " He answered, "The general, with tens of thousands of crack troops, surrendered at the mere rumor of his approach.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu replied, "You had tens of thousands of elite troops and submitted at the first rumor of his coming.

sentences.zh: 彼新得志，威震天下。

translations.literal: He has newly gained his aim and his prestige shakes the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He has just seized power; his prestige fills the empire.

sentences.zh: 三軍人情，都已去矣，廣陵豈可得至邪！

translations.literal: The hearts of the three armies have already left you; how could you possibly reach Guangling!
translations.idiomatic: Your soldiers' hearts are already gone—Guangling is beyond reach!

sentences.zh: 裕當反服還京口耳。

translations.literal: Yu will simply put on mourning garb and return to Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: As for me, I shall don mourning and go back to Jingkou.

sentences.zh: 」牢之叛走自縊死。

translations.literal: " Laozhi fled in rebellion and hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: " Laozhi rebelled, fled, and hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 何無忌謂高祖曰：「我將何之？

translations.literal: He Wuji said to Gaozu, "Where am I to go?
translations.idiomatic: He Wuji asked Gaozu, "Where should I go?

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「鎮北去必不免，卿可隨我還京口。

translations.literal: " Gaozu said, "The Pacifier of the North, if he goes, will surely not escape; you may follow me back to Jingkou.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu said, "Laozhi cannot flee and live; come back to Jingkou with me.

sentences.zh: 桓玄必能守節北面，我當與卿事之；

translations.literal: Huan Xuan will surely be able to hold to his duty and face north; I shall serve him with you;
translations.idiomatic: If Xuan keeps faith to the throne and faces north, we will serve him together;

sentences.zh: 不然，與卿圖之。

translations.literal: if not, we shall plot against him together.
translations.idiomatic: if not, we will plot against him together.

sentences.zh: 今方是玄矯情任算之日，必將用我輩也。

translations.literal: Now is precisely the day when Xuan puts on a show of feeling while calculating his moves; he is sure to make use of us.
translations.idiomatic: This is the moment when Xuan feigns sentiment and counts his moves—he is bound to employ us.

sentences.zh: 」桓玄從兄脩以撫軍鎮丹徒，以高祖為中兵參軍，軍、郡如故。

translations.literal: " Huan Xuan's cousin Xiu, as Pacifying General, garrisoned Dantu and made Gaozu Central Staff Officer, his army and commandery posts unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuan's cousin Xiu, holding the post of Pacifying General at Dantu, appointed Gaozu Central Staff Officer with his military and prefectural titles unchanged.

sentences.zh: 孫恩自奔敗之後，徒旅漸散，懼生見獲，乃於臨海投水死。

translations.literal: After Sun En's rout his followers gradually dispersed; fearing capture alive, he threw himself into the waters at Linhai and died.
translations.idiomatic: After his defeats En's followers melted away; fearing capture, he drowned himself in the sea off Linhai.

sentences.zh: 餘眾推恩妹夫盧循為主。

translations.literal: The remainder made En's brother-in-law Lu Xun their leader.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors set up En's brother-in-law Lu Xun as leader.

sentences.zh: 桓玄欲且緝寧東土，以循為永嘉太守。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan wished for the moment to pacify the eastern lands and appointed Xun Administrator of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan, seeking to quiet the east for the moment, named Xun administrator of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 循雖受命，而寇暴不已。

translations.literal: Though Xun accepted the appointment, his raids and violence did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Xun took office but never stopped his raids.

sentences.zh: 五月，玄復遣高祖東征。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Xuan again sent Gaozu on an eastern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Xuan again sent Gaozu east.

sentences.zh: 時循自臨海入東陽。

translations.literal: At that time Xun had entered Dongyang from Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: Xun had marched from Linhai into Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，玄復遣高祖破循於東陽。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year Xuan again sent Gaozu to defeat Xun at Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year Gaozu again defeated Xun at Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 循奔永嘉，復追破之，斬其大帥張士道，追討至于晉安，循浮海南走。

translations.literal: Xun fled to Yongjia; he was again pursued and defeated, and their great commander Zhang Shidao was beheaded; pursuit continued as far as Jin'an, and Xun fled south over the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Xun fled to Yongjia, was beaten again, and his commander Zhang Shidao was killed; pursuit reached Jin'an before Xun escaped south by sea.

sentences.zh: 六月，加高祖彭城內史。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Gaozu was additionally made Interior Governor of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he was also made interior governor of Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 桓玄為楚王，將謀篡盜。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan became Prince of Chu and plotted to usurp the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan became Prince of Chu and plotted usurpation.

sentences.zh: 玄從兄衞將軍謙屏人問高祖曰：「楚王勳德隆重，四海歸懷。

translations.literal: Xuan's cousin the Defender-General Qian dismissed the attendants and asked Gaozu, "The Prince of Chu's merit and virtue are weighty, and the realm turns to him.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Qian, Defender-General, sent attendants away and asked Gaozu, "The Prince of Chu's merit is immense and the world looks to him.

sentences.zh: 朝廷之情，咸謂宜有揖讓，卿意以為何如？

translations.literal: Court sentiment everywhere holds that there should be a yielding of the throne; what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: Everyone at court says he should receive the abdication—what is your view?

sentences.zh: 」高祖既志欲圖玄，乃遜辭答曰：「楚王，宣武之子，勳德蓋世。

translations.literal: " Gaozu, who already intended to plot against Xuan, answered with feigned modesty, "The Prince of Chu is a son of Emperor Xuanwu; his merit and virtue cover the age.
translations.idiomatic: " Gaozu, already planning against Xuan, answered evasively: "The Prince of Chu is a son of Emperor Xuanwu; his merit towers over the age.

sentences.zh: 晉室微弱，民望久移，乘運禪代，有何不可。

translations.literal: The house of Jin is feeble; the people's hopes have long shifted; to take the mandate in this turn of fortune—what could be impossible?
translations.idiomatic: Jin is weak and the people's hearts have long shifted; to accept the mandate in such a season—why not?

sentences.zh: 」謙喜曰：「卿謂可爾，便當是真可爾。

translations.literal: " Qian rejoiced and said, "If you say it can be done, then it truly can be done.
translations.idiomatic: " Qian was delighted: "If you say it is possible, then it truly is possible.

sentences.zh: 」十二月，桓玄篡帝位，遷天子於尋陽。

translations.literal: " In the twelfth month Huan Xuan usurped the imperial throne and moved the Son of Heaven to Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: " In the twelfth month Xuan seized the throne and moved the emperor to Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 桓脩入朝，高祖從至京邑。

translations.literal: Huan Xiu entered the court, and Gaozu accompanied him to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu went to court, and Gaozu went with him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 玄見高祖，謂司徒王謐曰：「昨見劉裕，風骨不恒，蓋人傑也。

translations.literal: Xuan saw Gaozu and said to the Minister over the Masses Wang Mi, "Yesterday I saw Liu Yu; his bearing is no ordinary man's—he is surely a hero of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan saw Gaozu and told Minister Wang Mi, "I saw Liu Yu yesterday—his bearing is extraordinary; he is a hero of the age.

sentences.zh: 」每遊集，輒引接慇懃，贈賜甚厚。

translations.literal: " Whenever they met at gatherings he would draw him close with earnest courtesy and bestow gifts in great abundance.
translations.idiomatic: " At every gathering he drew him close with warm courtesy and lavished gifts on him.

sentences.zh: 高祖愈惡之。

translations.literal: Gaozu hated this all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu loathed it all the more.

sentences.zh: 或說玄曰：「劉裕龍行虎步，視瞻不凡，恐不為人下，宜蚤為其所。

translations.literal: Someone said to Xuan, "Liu Yu walks like a dragon and tiger; his gaze is uncommon; I fear he will not remain beneath others—you should deal with him early.
translations.idiomatic: Someone warned Xuan, "Liu Yu moves like dragon and tiger; his look is uncommon—I fear he will not stay subordinate. Cut him down early.

sentences.zh: 」玄曰：「我方欲平蕩中原，非劉裕莫可付以大事。

translations.literal: " Xuan said, "I am just about to pacify the Central Plains; none but Liu Yu can be entrusted with a great commission.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuan said, "I mean to pacify the Central Plains, and only Liu Yu can be entrusted with so great a charge.

sentences.zh: 關、隴平定，然後當別議之耳。

translations.literal: When Guan and Long are pacified, then we may discuss the matter separately.
translations.idiomatic: Once Guan and Long are settled, we can take the matter up again.

sentences.zh: 」玄乃下詔曰：「劉裕以寡制眾，屢摧妖鋒。

translations.literal: " Xuan then issued an edict saying, "Liu Yu, with few men controlled many, and repeatedly shattered the demonic vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: " He then issued an edict: "Liu Yu, though outnumbered, has repeatedly broken the rebel spearhead.

sentences.zh: 汎海窮追，十殄其八。

translations.literal: He pursued them across the sea to the end; eight in ten were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: He chased them across the sea and destroyed eight in ten.

sentences.zh: 諸將力戰，多被重創。

translations.literal: The generals fought hard and many suffered grave wounds.
translations.idiomatic: His generals fought hard; many were gravely wounded.

sentences.zh: 自元帥以下至于將士，並宜論賞，以敍勳烈。」

translations.literal: From the commander-in-chief down to officers and soldiers, all should be rewarded in due measure to record their merit."
translations.idiomatic: From the commander down to the ranks, rewards are due to record their merit."

sentences.zh: 先是高祖東征盧循，何無忌隨至山陰，勸於會稽舉義。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Gaozu campaigned east against Lu Xun, He Wuji followed him to Shanyin and urged raising the standard of righteousness in Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, on the eastern campaign against Lu Xun, He Wuji had gone with him to Shanyin and urged an uprising in Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 高祖以為玄未據極位，且會稽遙遠，事濟為難，俟其篡逆事著，徐於京口圖之，不憂不剋。

translations.literal: Gaozu held that Xuan had not yet reached the supreme position, and that Kuaiji was far away and success hard to achieve; he would wait until Xuan's usurpation was manifest and then plot slowly at Jingkou—there was no worry of failure.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu thought Xuan had not yet seized the throne, Kuaiji was too remote, and success would be hard; he would wait until the usurpation was plain, then strike from Jingkou at leisure.

sentences.zh: 至是桓脩還京，高祖託以金創疾動，不堪步從，乃與無忌同船共還，建興復之計。

translations.literal: When Huan Xiu returned to the capital, Gaozu pleaded that a wound from metal had flared up and he could not keep pace on foot; he and Wuji then took the same boat back together and laid plans to restore the Jin.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiu returned to the capital, Gaozu claimed his old wound had reopened and he could not march; he sailed back with Wuji to plan Jin's restoration.

sentences.zh: 於是與弟道規、沛郡劉毅、平昌孟昶、任城魏詠之、高平檀憑之、琅邪諸葛長民、太原王元德、隴西辛扈興、東莞童厚之，並同義謀。

translations.literal: Thereupon with his younger brother Daogui, Liu Yi of Pei Commandery, Meng Chang of Pingchang, Wei Yongzhi of Rencheng, Tan Pingzhi of Gaoping, Zhuge Changmin of Langya, Wang Yuande of Taiyuan, Xin Huxing of Longxi, Tong Houzhi of Dongguan, and others, they joined in the righteous plot.
translations.idiomatic: He joined his brother Daogui, Liu Yi, Meng Chang, Wei Yongzhi, Tan Pingzhi, Zhuge Changmin, Wang Yuande, Xin Huxing, Tong Houzhi, and others in conspiracy.

sentences.zh: 時桓脩弟弘為征虜將軍、青州刺史，鎮廣陵。

translations.literal: At that time Xiu's younger brother Hong was General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Inspector of Qingzhou, garrisoning Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu's brother Hong was General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Qingzhou inspector, stationed at Guangling.

sentences.zh: 道規為弘中兵參軍，昶為州主簿。

translations.literal: Daogui was Hong's Central Staff Officer; Chang was the prefectural registrar.
translations.idiomatic: Daogui served on Hong's staff; Chang was registrar of the province.

sentences.zh: 乃令毅潛往就昶，聚徒於江北，謀起兵殺弘。

translations.literal: They ordered Yi to go secretly to join Chang, gather followers north of the river, and plan to raise troops and kill Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was sent secretly to Chang to raise men north of the Yangzi and kill Hong.

sentences.zh: 長民為豫州刺史刁逵左軍府參軍，謀據歷陽相應。

translations.literal: Changmin was a staff officer in the Left Headquarters of Inspector Diao Kui of Yuzhou and planned to hold Liyang in response.
translations.idiomatic: Changmin, on Diao Kui's staff in Yuzhou, would seize Liyang in concert.

sentences.zh: 元德、厚之謀於京邑聚眾攻玄，並剋期齊發。

translations.literal: Yuande and Houzhi planned to gather masses in the capital to attack Xuan, all with a fixed day to rise together.
translations.idiomatic: Yuande and Houzhi would rally men in the capital; all set the same day to strike.

sentences.zh: 三年二月己丑朔，乙卯，高祖託以遊獵，與無忌等收集義徒，凡同謀何無忌、魏詠之、詠之弟欣之、順之、檀憑之、憑之從子韶、韶弟祗、隆、道濟、[5]道濟從兄範之、高祖弟道憐、劉毅、毅從弟藩、孟昶、昶族弟懷玉、河內向彌、管義之、陳留周安穆、臨淮劉蔚、從弟珪之、東莞臧熹、[6]從弟寶符、從子穆生、童茂宗、陳郡周道民、漁陽田演、譙國范清等二十七人；

translations.literal: On the first day of the second month of the third year, on the day yimao, Gaozu pretended to go hunting and with Wuji and others gathered the righteous followers; the fellow conspirators numbered twenty-seven men—He Wuji, Wei Yongzhi, Yongzhi's brothers Xin and Shun, Tan Pingzhi, Pingzhi's clansman Shao, Shao's brothers Zhi and Long, Daoji, [5] Daoji's cousin Fan, Gaozu's brother Daolian, Liu Yi, Yi's cousin Fan, Meng Chang, Chang's clansman Huaiyu, Xiang Mi of Henei, Guan Yizhi, Zhou Anmu of Chenliu, Liu Wei of Huaiyin, Wei's cousin Guizhi, Zang Xi of Dongguan, [6] Xi's cousin Baofu, Xi's nephew Musheng, Tong Maozong, Zhou Daomin of Chen, Tian Yan of Yuyang, Fan Qing of Qiao, and others;
translations.idiomatic: On yimao of the second month, third year, Gaozu feigned a hunt and gathered conspirators—twenty-seven named men including Wuji, the Wei brothers, Tan Pingzhi and kin, Daogui and kin, Yi and kin, Chang and kin, Xiang Mi, Guan Yizhi, Zhou Anmu, Liu Wei and kin, Zang Xi and kin, Tong Maozong, Zhou Daomin, Tian Yan, Fan Qing, and others;

sentences.zh: 願從者百餘人。

translations.literal: those willing to follow numbered more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: more than a hundred volunteers joined them.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，詰旦，城開，無忌服傳詔服，稱詔居前。

translations.literal: On the day bingchen, at dawn, the gates opened; Wuji donned robes as if bearing an edict and, claiming an imperial command, went before the rest.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on bingchen the gates opened; Wuji wore courier robes and claimed an edict as he led the way.

sentences.zh: 義眾馳入，齊聲大呼，吏士驚散，莫敢動，即斬脩以徇。

translations.literal: The righteous masses galloped in, shouting together; officials and soldiers scattered in alarm and none dared move; they at once beheaded Xiu and displayed his head.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels rushed in with a great shout; the garrison fled; Xiu was beheaded and his head displayed.

sentences.zh: 高祖哭甚慟，厚加殯斂。

translations.literal: Gaozu wept with extreme grief and gave him lavish funeral rites.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu wept bitterly and gave him a lavish burial.

sentences.zh: 孟昶勸弘其日出獵。

translations.literal: Meng Chang urged Hong to go out hunting that very day.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Chang urged Hong to hunt that same day.

sentences.zh: 未明開門，出獵人，昶、道規、毅等率壯士五六十人因開門直入。

translations.literal: Before dawn the gates opened for the hunting party; Chang, Daogui, Yi, and others led fifty or sixty stalwarts and entered straight through the opened gates.
translations.idiomatic: Before dawn the hunt party left; Chang, Daogui, Yi, and fifty-odd men slipped in as the gates opened.

sentences.zh: 弘方噉粥，即斬之，因收眾濟江。

translations.literal: Hong was just eating gruel when they beheaded him; they then gathered the troops and crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: Hong was at his porridge when they killed him, rallied the men, and crossed the river.

sentences.zh: 義軍初剋京城，脩司馬刁弘率文武佐吏來赴。

translations.literal: When the righteous army first took the capital, Xiu's registrar Diao Hong led civil and military aides to come to their aid.
translations.idiomatic: As the rebels secured the capital, Diao Hong, Xiu's registrar, marched up with officials and troops.

sentences.zh: 高祖登城謂之曰：「郭江州已奉乘輿反正於尋陽，我等並被密詔，誅除逆黨，同會今日。

translations.literal: Gaozu mounted the wall and said to him, "Inspector Guo of Jiangzhou has already received the imperial carriage and turned to righteousness at Xunyang; we too have all received secret edicts to exterminate the rebel faction and assemble on this day.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu mounted the wall: "Inspector Guo at Jiangzhou has already restored the emperor at Xunyang; we hold secret orders to purge traitors today.

sentences.zh: 賊玄之首，已當梟於大航矣。

translations.literal: The rebel Xuan's head should already be spiked at the Great Ferry.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's head should already hang at the Great Ferry."

sentences.zh: 諸君非大晉之臣乎，今來欲何為？

translations.literal: Are you not ministers of great Jin—what have you come for now?
translations.idiomatic: You are ministers of Jin—what do you want here?"

sentences.zh: 」弘等信之，收眾而退。

translations.literal: " Hong and the others believed him and withdrew their forces.
translations.idiomatic: Hong believed him and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 毅既至，高祖命誅弘。

translations.literal: When Yi arrived, Gaozu ordered Hong executed.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi arrived, Gaozu had Hong killed.

sentences.zh: 毅兄邁先在京師，事未發數日，高祖遣同謀周安穆報之，使為內應。

translations.literal: Yi's elder brother Mai was already in the capital; several days before the affair Gaozu sent fellow conspirator Zhou Anmu to report to him and make him an inside contact.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's brother Mai was in the capital; days before, Gaozu sent Zhou Anmu to enlist him inside.

sentences.zh: 邁外雖酬許，內甚震懼。

translations.literal: Outwardly Mai answered agreeably, but inwardly he was greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Mai agreed outwardly but was terrified within.

sentences.zh: 安穆見其惶駭，慮事必泄，乃馳歸。

translations.literal: Anmu saw his panic and, fearing the affair would leak, galloped back.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his panic, Anmu feared exposure and rode back at once.

sentences.zh: 時玄以邁為竟陵太守，邁不知所為，便下船欲之郡。

translations.literal: At that time Xuan had made Mai Administrator of Jingling; not knowing what to do, Mai boarded a boat intending to go to his commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan had named Mai administrator of Jingling; bewildered, Mai boarded a boat for his post.

sentences.zh: 是夜，玄與邁書曰：「北府人情云何？

translations.literal: That night Xuan wrote to Mai, "How stand the feelings of the men of the Northern Headquarters?
translations.idiomatic: That night Xuan wrote: "What is the mood in the Northern Headquarters?

sentences.zh: 卿近見劉裕何所道？

translations.literal: What did Liu Yu say when you saw him recently?
translations.idiomatic: What did Liu Yu say when you met him?"

sentences.zh: 」邁謂玄已知其謀，晨起白之。

translations.literal: " Mai thought Xuan already knew of the plot; at dawn he went to report it.
translations.idiomatic: Mai thought himself discovered and reported at dawn.

sentences.zh: 玄驚懼，封邁為重安侯；

translations.literal: Xuan was alarmed and in fear enfeoffed Mai as Marquis of Chong'an;
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Xuan made Mai Marquis of Chong'an;

sentences.zh: 既而嫌邁不執安穆，使得逃去，[7]乃殺之。

translations.literal: then, resenting that Mai had not seized Anmu and let him escape, [7] he killed him.
translations.idiomatic: then, angry Mai had let Anmu escape, [7] he killed him.

sentences.zh: 誅元德、扈興、厚之等。

translations.literal: He executed Yuande, Huxing, Houzhi, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He executed Yuande, Huxing, Houzhi, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 召桓謙、卞範之等謀拒高祖。

translations.literal: He summoned Huan Qian, Bian Fanzhi, and others to plan resisting Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: He called Qian, Bian Fanzhi, and others to plan defense.

sentences.zh: 謙等曰：「亟遣兵擊之。

translations.literal: Qian and the others said, "Send troops at once to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: They urged immediate attack.

sentences.zh: 」玄曰：「不然。

translations.literal: " Xuan said, "That will not do.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuan refused: "No.

sentences.zh: 彼兵速銳，計出萬死。

translations.literal: Their troops are swift and sharp; their plan is born of ten thousand deaths.
translations.idiomatic: They are swift and desperate—fighting for their lives.

sentences.zh: 若行遣水軍，不足相抗，如有蹉跌，則彼氣成而吾事敗矣。

translations.literal: If we send the navy it will not be enough to resist them; if there is any slip, their spirit will rise and our cause will fail.
translations.idiomatic: The fleet alone cannot stop them; one setback will steel them and ruin us.

sentences.zh: 不如屯大眾於覆舟山以待之。

translations.literal: Better mass a great host on Fuzhou Mountain and wait for them.
translations.idiomatic: Better mass troops on Fuzhou Mountain and wait.

sentences.zh: 彼空行二百里，無所措手，銳氣已挫，既至，忽見大軍，必驚懼駭愕。

translations.literal: They will have marched two hundred li with nothing to grasp; their sharp spirit will already be blunted; when they arrive and suddenly see a great army, they will surely be shocked and terrified.
translations.idiomatic: After two hundred li with no foothold their edge will dull; a great host will terrify them.

sentences.zh: 我案兵堅陣，勿與交鋒，彼求戰不得，自然散走。

translations.literal: We hold our ranks firm and do not join battle; unable to obtain a fight, they will naturally scatter and flee.
translations.idiomatic: Hold the line without fighting; denied battle, they will melt away.

sentences.zh: 此計之上也。

translations.literal: This is the supreme plan.
translations.idiomatic: That is the best plan."

sentences.zh: 」謙等固請，乃遣頓丘太守吳甫之、右衞將軍皇甫敷北拒義軍。

translations.literal: Qian and the others pressed firmly, and he then sent Administrator of Dunqiu Wu Fuzhi and Defender of the Right Huangfu Fu north to resist the righteous army.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed by Qian, he sent Wu Fuzhi and Huangfu Fu north against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 玄自聞軍起，憂懼無復為計。

translations.literal: From the time Xuan heard the army had risen, worry and fear left him no further plan.
translations.idiomatic: From the first news of revolt, Xuan was paralyzed with fear.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「劉裕等眾力甚弱，豈辦之有成，陛下何慮之甚。

translations.literal: Someone said, "Liu Yu and the others are very weak in numbers—how could they succeed? Why does Your Majesty worry so greatly?
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "Liu Yu's band is tiny—why such fear?"

sentences.zh: 」玄曰：「劉裕足為一世之雄；

translations.literal: " Xuan said, "Liu Yu is fully the hero of an age;
translations.idiomatic: " Xuan said, "Liu Yu is a hero of the age;

sentences.zh: 劉毅家無擔石之儲，摴蒲一擲百萬；

translations.literal: Liu Yi has not a picul of grain at home yet stakes a million on dice;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi is penniless yet stakes millions at dice;

sentences.zh: 何無忌，劉牢之甥，酷似其舅。

translations.literal: He Wuji is Liu Laozhi's nephew and greatly resembles his uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji is Laozhi's nephew and his very image.

sentences.zh: 共舉大事，何謂無成。」

translations.literal: Together they undertake a great affair—how can you say they will not succeed?"
translations.idiomatic: Together they attempt great things—how say they cannot succeed?"

sentences.zh: 眾推高祖為盟主，移檄京邑，曰：

translations.literal: The masses pushed Gaozu as covenant lord; he issued a proclamation to the capital, saying:
translations.idiomatic: They made Gaozu covenant lord and issued a proclamation to the capital:

sentences.zh: 夫治亂相因，理不常泰，狡焉肆虐，或值聖明。

translations.literal: Order and disorder follow upon one another; reason does not long abide in peace; when the crafty run riot, sometimes they meet a sage ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Order and chaos alternate; peace cannot last; when villains run wild, a sage ruler may yet appear.

sentences.zh: 自我大晉，陽九屢構，隆安以來，難結皇室，忠臣碎於虎口，貞良弊於豺狼。

translations.literal: Since our great Jin, the yang ninths have repeatedly come; from Long'an onward calamities have bound the imperial house—loyal ministers crushed in tigers' jaws, the upright ruined by wolves.
translations.idiomatic: Since Jin's founding, repeated calamities have struck; from Long'an loyal men were devoured and the good destroyed by wolves.

sentences.zh: 逆臣桓玄，陵虐人鬼，阻兵荊郢，肆暴都邑。

translations.literal: The rebel minister Huan Xuan tyrannized men and ghosts, blocked arms in Jing and Ying, and wantoned in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Huan Xuan oppressed heaven and earth, held Jing and Ying by force, and ravaged the capital.

sentences.zh: 天未亡難，凶力繁興，踰年之間，遂傾皇祚。

translations.literal: Heaven had not yet ended the affliction, but the villain's power flourished; within a year he overturned the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven had not abandoned Jin, yet within a year he seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 主上播越，流幸非所，神器沉淪，七廟毀墜。

translations.literal: The sovereign was driven afar, drifting to places not his own; the sacred vessel sank in the depths and the seven temples were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was driven into exile; the regalia were lost and the ancestral temples ruined.

sentences.zh: 夏后之罹浞、豷，有漢之遭莽、卓，方之於玄，未足為喻。

translations.literal: The calamities of Xia at Zhen and Yi, of Han at Wang Mang and Dong Zhuo—compared with Xuan they are not enough for a likeness.
translations.idiomatic: Xia's suffering under Zhen and Yi, Han's under Wang Mang and Dong Zhuo—Xuan surpasses them all.

sentences.zh: 自玄纂逆，于今歷年，亢旱彌時，民無生氣。

translations.literal: Since Xuan usurped, years have passed; drought has lasted long and the people have no breath of life.
translations.idiomatic: Since the usurpation, drought has lingered and the people are breathless.

sentences.zh: 加以士庶疲於轉輸，文武困於造築，父子乖離，室家分散，豈唯大東有杼軸之悲，摽梅有傾筐之塈而已哉。

translations.literal: In addition gentry and commoners are worn out by transport, civil and military by construction; fathers and sons are torn apart and families scattered—is it only the grief of the eastern states at the loom, or maidens with overturned baskets of mulberries?
translations.idiomatic: Gentry and soldiers are broken by levies and building; families are torn apart—not only the east laments at the loom or maidens their empty baskets.

sentences.zh: 仰觀天文，俯察人事，此而能久，孰有可亡。

translations.literal: Looking up at heaven's signs and down at human affairs—if this can long endure, what could perish?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth proclaim that such rule cannot endure.

sentences.zh: 凡在有心，誰不扼腕。

translations.literal: All who have a heart—who does not clench his fist?
translations.idiomatic: Every loyal heart clenches with rage.

sentences.zh: 裕等所以叩心泣血，不遑啟處者也。

translations.literal: This is why Yu and his fellows beat their breasts and weep blood and have no leisure to rest.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore we beat our breasts and cannot rest.

sentences.zh: 是故夕寐宵興，援獎忠烈，潛搆崎嶇，險過履虎。

translations.literal: Therefore we rise at nightfall and sleep at dawn, aiding and encouraging the loyal and brave, secretly building on rugged paths more perilous than treading tigers.
translations.idiomatic: We rise at dusk and sleep at dawn, aiding the loyal on paths more dangerous than treading tigers.

sentences.zh: 輔國將軍劉毅、廣武將軍何無忌、鎮北主簿孟昶、兗州主簿魏詠之、寧遠將軍劉道規、龍驤將軍劉藩、振威將軍檀憑之等，忠烈斷金，精貫白日，荷戈奮袂，志在畢命。

translations.literal: Assistant-General Liu Yi, General of Broad Martial He Wuji, Registrar Meng Chang, Registrar Wei Yongzhi, General of Pacifying the Distance Liu Daogui, General of the Dragon Cavalry Liu Fan, General Who Quells Might Tan Pingzhi, and others—their loyalty cleaves metal, their spirit pierces the sun; bearing weapons they spring forward, resolved to die to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, Wuji, Chang, Yongzhi, Daogui, Fan, Pingzhi, and others—loyal as cleaving metal, bright as the sun—take up arms resolved to die.

sentences.zh: 益州刺史毛璩，萬里齊契，掃定荊楚。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yizhou Mao Jin, in accord ten thousand li away, sweeps and settles Jing and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Jin of Yizhou marches in concert to sweep Jing and Chu.

sentences.zh: 江州刺史郭昶之，奉迎主上，宮于尋陽。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jiangzhou Guo Chaizhi receives and escorts the sovereign, housing him at Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chaizhi of Jiangzhou receives the emperor at Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 鎮北參軍王元德等，並率部曲，保據石頭。

translations.literal: Staff officer Wang Yuande and others each lead their detachments and hold Shitou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuande and others hold Shitou with their bands.

sentences.zh: 揚武將軍諸葛長民，收集義士，已據歷陽。

translations.literal: General of Martial Propagation Zhuge Changmin has gathered righteous men and already holds Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Changmin has gathered allies and holds Liyang.

sentences.zh: 征虜參軍庾賾之等，潛相連結，以為內應。

translations.literal: Staff officer Yu Yizhi and others secretly link together as inside contacts.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yizhi and others conspire within.

sentences.zh: 同力協規，所在蜂起，即日斬偽徐州刺史安城王脩、青州刺史弘首。

translations.literal: With united strength and shared plans, uprisings blaze everywhere; that very day the false Inspector of Xuzhou, Prince of Ancheng Xiu, and the Inspector of Qingzhou Hong were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: All rise together; that day the false prince Xiu and Hong were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 義眾既集，文武爭先，咸謂不有一統，則事無以輯。

translations.literal: The righteous masses having assembled, civil and military vie to be first; all say that without a single command nothing can be brought together.
translations.idiomatic: With the army gathered, all agree a single command is needed.

sentences.zh: 裕辭不獲已，遂總軍要。

translations.literal: Yu declined but could not refuse and then took overall military authority.
translations.idiomatic: Yu declined but accepted overall command.

sentences.zh: 庶上憑祖宗之靈，下罄義夫之力，剪馘逋逆，蕩清京輦。

translations.literal: May we rely above on the spirits of the ancestors and below exhaust the strength of the righteous, to cut down and destroy the fleeing rebels and sweep clear the capital.
translations.idiomatic: May we lean on our ancestors and the righteous to purge the capital.

sentences.zh: 公侯諸君，或世樹忠貞，或身荷爵寵，而並俛眉猾豎，自効莫由，顧瞻周道，寧不弔乎！

translations.literal: Lords and gentlemen, some for generations have planted loyalty, some personally bear enfeoffed favor, yet all bow to the crafty villain with no way to serve—gazing on the Zhou way, can you not mourn!
translations.idiomatic: You who bear hereditary loyalty or personal favor yet bow to the usurper—do you not mourn for the dynasty?

sentences.zh: 今日之舉，良其會也。

translations.literal: Today's rising is truly the occasion.
translations.idiomatic: Today is your hour.

sentences.zh: 裕以虛薄，才非古人，勢接於已踐之機，受任於既頹之運。

translations.literal: Yu is shallow and slight, his talent not that of men of old; the momentum meets a moment already trodden, and the charge comes in a fortune already failing.
translations.idiomatic: Yu is unworthy and untimely, thrust forward as the realm totters.

sentences.zh: 丹誠未宣，感慨憤躍，望霄漢以永懷，眄山川以增厲。

translations.literal: Sincerity not yet declared, he is moved by indignant leaping; he gazes at the Milky Way in everlasting longing and looks on mountains and rivers to increase sternness.
translations.idiomatic: His heart burns with loyalty; he looks to heaven and stiffens at the sight of his land.

sentences.zh: 授檄之日，神馳賊廷。

translations.literal: On the day the proclamation was handed out, his spirit flew to the rebel court.
translations.idiomatic: The day the proclamation went forth, his thoughts were already at the enemy capital.

sentences.zh: 以孟昶為長史，總攝後事；

translations.literal: Meng Chang was made Chief Clerk to oversee affairs in the rear;
translations.idiomatic: Meng Chang became chief clerk for the rear;

sentences.zh: 檀憑之為司馬。

translations.literal: Tan Pingzhi was made Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Pingzhi became marshal.

sentences.zh: 百姓願從者千餘人。

translations.literal: Common people wishing to follow numbered more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand civilians joined them.

sentences.zh: 三月戊午朔，遇吳甫之於江乘。

translations.literal: On the first day of the third month, on the day wuwu, they met Wu Fuzhi at Jiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu, the first of the third month, they met Wu Fuzhi at Jiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 甫之，玄驍將也，其兵甚銳。

translations.literal: Fuzhi was a fierce general of Xuan's, and his troops were very sharp.
translations.idiomatic: Fuzhi was Xuan's fierce general; his troops were elite.

sentences.zh: 高祖躬執長刀，大呼以衝之，眾皆披靡，即斬甫之。

translations.literal: Gaozu himself grasped a long blade and shouted as he charged; all were overthrown, and Fuzhi was beheaded at once.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu charged with a long saber shouting; the enemy broke; Fuzhi was killed.

sentences.zh: 進至羅落橋，皇甫敷率數千人逆戰。

translations.literal: Advancing to Luoluo Bridge, Huangfu Fu led several thousand men to meet them in battle.
translations.idiomatic: At Luoluo Bridge, Huangfu Fu met them with thousands.

sentences.zh: 寧遠將軍檀憑之與高祖各御一隊，憑之戰敗見殺，其眾退散。

translations.literal: General of Pacifying the Distance Tan Pingzhi and Gaozu each commanded a column; Pingzhi was defeated in battle and killed, and his masses scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Pingzhi and Gaozu each led a wing; Pingzhi was killed and his men scattered.

sentences.zh: 高祖進戰彌厲，前後奮擊，應時摧破，即斬敷首。

translations.literal: Gaozu pressed the battle ever harder, striking before and behind; as the moment demanded he shattered them and beheaded Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu fought harder, struck front and rear, and killed Fu.

sentences.zh: 初高祖與何無忌等共建大謀，有善相者相高祖及無忌等並當大貴，其應甚近，惟云憑之無相。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Gaozu and He Wuji and others together laid the great plan, a skilled physiognomist read Gaozu and Wuji and the rest as all destined for great nobility, the fulfillment very near—only Pingzhi, he said, had no such aspect.
translations.idiomatic: When they first plotted, a physiognomist said Gaozu, Wuji, and the rest would soon rise high—only Pingzhi lacked the mark.

sentences.zh: 高祖與無忌密相謂曰：「吾等既為同舟，理無偏異。

translations.literal: Gaozu and Wuji secretly said to each other, "We are in the same boat and reason admits no partiality.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu and Wuji whispered, "We share one boat; fortune must be shared.

sentences.zh: 吾徒咸皆富貴，則檀不應獨殊。

translations.literal: If we are all to be rich and noble, Tan should not alone be unlike the rest.
translations.idiomatic: If we rise, Tan should not be left out."

sentences.zh: 」深不解相者之言。

translations.literal: " They deeply did not understand the physiognomist's words.
translations.idiomatic: They could not understand the seer.

sentences.zh: 至是而憑之戰死，高祖知其事必捷。

translations.literal: When Pingzhi died in battle, Gaozu knew the affair would surely succeed.
translations.idiomatic: When Pingzhi fell, Gaozu knew victory was assured.

sentences.zh: 玄聞敷等並沒，愈懼。

translations.literal: Xuan heard that Fu and the others were all destroyed and grew more afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Fu was dead, Xuan grew more afraid.

sentences.zh: 使桓謙屯東陵口，卞範之屯覆舟山西，眾合二萬。

translations.literal: He sent Huan Qian to encamp at Dongling Ford and Bian Fanzhi west of Fuzhou Mountain; their masses together numbered twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He posted Qian at Dongling Ford and Fanzhi west of Fuzhou Mountain—twenty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 己未旦，義軍食畢，棄其餘糧，進至覆舟山東，使丐士張旗幟於山上，以為疑兵。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei at dawn, the righteous army finished eating, cast aside their remaining grain, advanced to the east of Fuzhou Mountain, and had beggar soldiers raise banners on the hill as a decoy force.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on jiwei they ate, left surplus grain, marched east of Fuzhou Mountain, and posted beggars with flags on the hill as a feint.

sentences.zh: 玄又遣武騎將軍庾禕之，[8]配以精卒利器，助謙等。

translations.literal: Xuan again sent General of Martial Cavalry Yu Yizhi, [8] equipping him with elite troops and sharp weapons to assist Qian and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan sent Yu Yizhi, [8] General of Martial Cavalry, with picked troops and fine arms to reinforce Qian.

sentences.zh: 高祖躬先士卒以奔之，將士皆殊死戰，無不一當百，呼聲動天地。

translations.literal: Gaozu personally led the troops in the charge; officers and soldiers all fought to the death, each one matched a hundred; their shouting shook heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu led the charge himself; his men fought as if each were worth a hundred, and their battle cry shook heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 時東北風急，因命縱火，煙爓張天，鼓噪之音震京邑。

translations.literal: At that time the northeast wind blew hard; he therefore ordered fire set; smoke and flames filled the sky; the sound of drums and shouts shook the capital.
translations.idiomatic: A fierce northeast wind was blowing; Gaozu ordered the field set ablaze. Smoke blotted out the sky, and the roar of drums and war cries shook the capital.

sentences.zh: 謙等諸軍，一時土崩。

translations.literal: Qian's and the other armies at once collapsed like earthen walls.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's lines collapsed all at once.

sentences.zh: 玄始雖遣軍置陣，而走意已決，別使領軍將軍殷仲文具舟於石頭，仍將子姪浮江南走。

translations.literal: At first Xuan had sent troops to form battle lines, but his intention to flee was already fixed; he separately sent General Who Attends the Army Yin Zhongwen to prepare boats at Shitou, and then took his sons and nephews south across the river by boat.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xuan had deployed his army, he had already decided to run. He sent Yin Zhongwen to ready boats at Shitou, then fled south across the river with his sons and nephews.

sentences.zh: 庚申，高祖鎮石頭城，立留臺官，[9]焚桓溫神主於宣陽門外，造晉新主，立于太廟。

translations.literal: On gengshen, Gaozu garrisoned Shitou fortress, established officials of the rear capital, [9] burned Huan Wen's spirit tablet outside Xuanyang Gate, made new tablets for Jin, and installed them in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Gaozu held Shitou, set up a rear capital administration, [9] burned Huan Wen's spirit tablet outside Xuanyang Gate, and installed new Jin tablets in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 遣諸將帥追玄，尚書王嘏率百官奉迎乘輿。

translations.literal: He sent generals to pursue Xuan; Secretary Wang Gu led the hundred officials to welcome the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: He sent generals in pursuit of Xuan while Secretary Wang Gu led the officials to welcome the emperor home.

sentences.zh: [10]司徒王謐與眾議推高祖領揚州，固辭。

translations.literal: [10] Regent Wang Mi and the assembly discussed recommending Gaozu to head Yang Province; he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: [10] Regent Wang Mi and the court proposed that Gaozu take Yang Province; he firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 乃以謐為錄尚書事，領揚州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon Mi was made Recorder of the Affairs of the Masters of Writing and Inspector of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Mi was then made Recorder of the Masters of Writing and Inspector of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 於是推高祖為使持節、都督揚、徐、兗、豫、青、冀、幽、并八州諸軍事、領軍將軍、徐州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon Gaozu was recommended as Bearer of the Staff with Full Powers, Commander-in-Chief of the Military Affairs of the Eight Provinces of Yang, Xu, Yan, Yu, Qing, Ji, You, and Bing, General Who Attends the Army, and Inspector of Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was then appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of eight provinces, General Who Attends the Army, and Inspector of Xu Province.

translations.literal: Editorial note eleven.
translations.idiomatic: See editorial note eleven.

sentences.zh: 先是朝廷承晉氏亂政，百司縱弛，桓玄雖欲釐整，而眾莫從之。

translations.literal: Earlier the court had inherited the disorderly government of the Jin house; the hundred offices were lax; although Huan Xuan wished to rectify and restore order, the multitude would not follow him.
translations.idiomatic: The court still bore the legacy of Jin's disorder: every office was slack. Huan Xuan tried to impose discipline, but no one would obey.

sentences.zh: 高祖以身範物，先以威禁內外，百官皆肅然奉職，二三日間，風俗頓改。

translations.literal: Gaozu took his person as the model for things; first by authority he forbade misconduct within and without; all officials respectfully attended their duties; within two or three days customs abruptly changed.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu led by example and enforced discipline at court and beyond. Within days every official stood to duty, and public conduct changed overnight.

sentences.zh: 且桓玄雖以雄豪見推，而一朝便有極位，晉氏四方牧守及在朝大臣，盡心伏事，臣主之分定矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, although Huan Xuan was promoted for his bold heroism, in a single morning he reached the supreme position; the Jin house's governors and prefects in all directions and the great ministers at court all devoted their hearts to serving him—the distinction between minister and sovereign was already fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan had risen overnight to supreme power, and every governor and minister in the land had already accepted him as sovereign.

sentences.zh: 高祖位微於朝，眾無一旅，奮臂草萊之中，倡大義以復皇祚。

translations.literal: Gaozu's rank was low at court; his followers did not amount to a single brigade; he raised his arm from among the common grasses, and proclaimed the great principle to restore the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu held no high rank and commanded barely a brigade, yet from the common ranks he raised the banner of restoring the throne.

sentences.zh: 由是王謐等諸人時失民望，[12]莫不愧而憚焉。

translations.literal: Hence Wang Mi and others at the time had lost the people's expectation; [12] none were not ashamed and in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi and the rest had lost the people's trust; [12] all were ashamed and afraid.

sentences.zh: 諸葛長民失期不得發，刁逵執送之，未至而玄敗。

translations.literal: Zhuge Changmin missed the appointed date and could not launch; Diao Kui arrested and sent him under escort; before he arrived Xuan was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Changmin missed his rendezvous and was seized by Diao Kui for transport to the capital; before he arrived, Xuan was already defeated.

sentences.zh: 玄經尋陽，江州刺史郭昶之備乘輿法物資之。

translations.literal: When Xuan passed through Xunyang, Inspector of Jiang Province Guo Changzhi prepared the imperial carriage and ritual regalia to supply him.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Xunyang, Xuan was supplied with the imperial carriage and regalia by Jiangzhou Inspector Guo Changzhi.

sentences.zh: 玄收略得二千餘人，挾天子走江陵。

translations.literal: Xuan gathered about two thousand more men and fled with the Son of Heaven to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan scraped together two thousand more men and fled to Jiangling with the emperor in tow.

sentences.zh: 冠軍將軍劉毅、輔國將軍何無忌、振武將軍劉道規率諸軍追討。

translations.literal: Champion-General Liu Yi, General Who Assists the State He Wuji, and General Who Quells Might Liu Daogui led the armies in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Champion-General Liu Yi, He Wuji, and Liu Daogui led the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射王愉、愉子荊州刺史綏等，江左冠族。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Yu, Yu's son Inspector of Jing Province Sui, and others were the leading clans of the lands east of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Wang Yu, his son Jingzhou Inspector Sui, and their kin were among the greatest families south of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 綏少有重名，以高祖起自布衣，甚相凌忽。

translations.literal: Sui from youth had a great reputation; because Gaozu had risen from common cloth, he greatly looked down on and neglected him.
translations.idiomatic: Sui had been famous since youth and looked down on Gaozu as a man risen from the ranks.

sentences.zh: 綏，桓氏甥，亦有自疑之志。

translations.literal: Sui, being a nephew of the Huan clan, also harbored thoughts of self-doubt.
translations.idiomatic: As a nephew of the Huan clan, Sui also feared for himself.

sentences.zh: 高祖悉誅之。

translations.literal: Gaozu executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu had them all executed.

sentences.zh: 四月，奉武陵王遵為大將軍，承制。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, they invested Prince of Wuling Zun as Grand General and authorized him to wield imperial authority.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Prince of Wuling Zun was made Grand General with authority to act in the emperor's name.

sentences.zh: 大赦天下，唯桓玄一祖後不在赦例。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm; only the descendants of Huan Xuan's founding ancestor were excluded.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was declared, excluding only the line of Huan Xuan's founding ancestor.

sentences.zh: 初高祖家貧，嘗負刁逵社錢三萬，經時無以還。

translations.literal: Initially Gaozu's family was poor; he once owed Diao Kui thirty thousand in community-loan money and for a long time had no means to repay.
translations.idiomatic: In his early poverty Gaozu owed Diao Kui thirty thousand in community-loan money and could not repay it for a long time.

sentences.zh: 逵執錄甚嚴，王謐造逵見之，密以錢代還，由是得釋。

translations.literal: Kui's enforcement of the debt was very strict; Wang Mi visited Kui and secretly repaid the money on his behalf; thus he was released.
translations.idiomatic: Kui pressed the debt hard until Wang Mi visited him in secret and paid it off, freeing Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 高祖名微位薄，盛流皆不與相知，唯謐交焉。

translations.literal: Gaozu's fame was slight and his rank low; the great currents of society all would not associate with him; only Mi befriended him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was obscure and lowly; the great families would not know him—only Mi befriended him.

sentences.zh: 桓玄將篡，謐手解安帝璽紱，為玄佐命功臣。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan was about to usurp, Mi with his own hands removed Emperor An's seal and cord, becoming a meritorious minister who aided Xuan's mandate.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan seized the throne, Mi himself removed Emperor An's seal and cord and became one of Xuan's chief supporters.

sentences.zh: 及義旗建，眾並謂謐宜誅，唯高祖保持之。

translations.literal: When the righteous banner was raised, all said Mi should be executed; only Gaozu protected him.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army rose, everyone said Mi should die; only Gaozu shielded him.

sentences.zh: 劉毅嘗因朝會，問謐璽紱所在，謐益懼。

translations.literal: Liu Yi once at a court assembly asked Mi where the seal and cord were; Mi grew all the more fearful.
translations.idiomatic: At court Liu Yi once asked Mi where the imperial seal and cord were; Mi grew still more afraid.

sentences.zh: 及王愉父子誅，謐從弟諶謂謐曰：「王駒無罪，而義旗誅之，此是剪除勝己，以絕民望。

translations.literal: When Wang Yu and his son were executed, Mi's cousin Zhen said to Mi: "Lord Jiao was innocent, yet the righteous army executed him—this is cutting down those who surpass oneself, to cut off the people's hopes.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Yu and his son were killed, Mi's cousin Zhen warned him: "Lord Jiao was innocent, yet the righteous army killed him. That is how rivals are removed and popular hopes extinguished.

sentences.zh: 兄既桓氏黨附，名位如此，欲求免得乎？

translations.literal: Elder brother, being attached to the Huan faction with fame and rank such as this—do you think you can seek to be spared?
translations.idiomatic: You are a Huan partisan with rank like yours—do you think you can escape?"

sentences.zh: 」駒，愉小字也。

translations.literal: " Jiao was Yu's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: "Jiao" was Yu's childhood name.

sentences.zh: 謐懼，奔于曲阿。

translations.literal: In fear Mi fled to Qu'a.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Mi fled to Qu'a.

sentences.zh: 高祖牋白大將軍，深相保謐，迎還復位。

translations.literal: Gaozu wrote to the Grand General, pledging to protect Mi deeply, and welcomed him back to resume his position.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu wrote the Grand General pledging to protect Mi and brought him back to office.

sentences.zh: 光祿勳卞承之、[13]左衞將軍褚粲、游擊將軍司馬秀役使官人，為御史中丞王禎之所糾察，謝牋言辭怨憤。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Bian Chengzhi, [13] Left Guard General Chu Can, and General of Agile Cavalry Sima Xiu used officials as servants; they were investigated by Inspector of Censors Wang Zhenzhi; their memorials of apology were resentful and angry in tone.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Bian Chengzhi, [13] Left Guard General Chu Can, and General of Agile Cavalry Sima Xiu had abused subordinates. Censor Wang Zhenzhi impeached them, and their apologies were bitter and defiant.

sentences.zh: 承之造司宜藏。

translations.literal: Chengzhi went to the Judicial Office intending to hide.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzhi fled to the Judicial Office to hide.

sentences.zh: 高祖與大將軍牋，白「粲等備位大臣，所懷必盡。

translations.literal: Gaozu wrote to the Grand General, stating: "Can and the others hold ministerial rank and should have expressed their grievances fully.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu wrote the Grand General: "Can and the others are great ministers and should have stated their case plainly.

sentences.zh: 執憲不允，自應據理陳訴，而橫興怨忿，歸咎有司。

translations.literal: In enforcing the law they were not permitted; they should have appealed according to reason, yet they wantonly gave rise to resentment and shifted blame onto the officials in charge.
translations.idiomatic: Denied by the censors, they should have appealed on the merits instead of venting rage at the investigating officers.

sentences.zh: 宜加裁當，以清風軌」。

translations.literal: They should receive appropriate discipline to clear the standards of conduct."
translations.idiomatic: They deserve proper punishment to restore discipline."

sentences.zh: 並免官。

translations.literal: All were dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: All were removed from office.

sentences.zh: 桓玄兄子歆，[14]聚眾向歷陽，高祖命輔國將軍諸葛長民擊走之。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan's nephew's son Xin, [14] gathered masses and marched on Liyang; Gaozu ordered General Who Assists the State Zhuge Changmin to attack and drive him off.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan's grand-nephew Xin, [14] raised troops against Liyang; Gaozu sent Zhuge Changmin to drive him off.

sentences.zh: 無忌、道規破玄大將郭銓等于桑落洲，[15]眾軍進據尋陽。

translations.literal: Wuji and Daogui defeated Xuan's great general Guo Qian and others at Sangluo Isle, [15] and the armies advanced to occupy Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji and Daogui routed Guo Qian at Sangluo Isle, [15] and the army took Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 加高祖都督江州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Gaozu was additionally made Commander-in-Chief of the Military Affairs of Jiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was additionally made Commander-in-Chief of Jiang Province.

sentences.zh: 玄既還荊郢，大聚兵眾，召水軍造樓船、器械，率眾二萬，挾天子發江陵，浮江東下，與冠軍將軍劉毅等相遇於崢嶸洲，眾軍下擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Xuan, having returned to Jing and Ying, massed troops greatly, summoned the navy to build tower ships and engines, led twenty thousand men, took the Son of Heaven with him from Jiangling, floated down the river eastward, and met Champion-General Liu Yi and others at Zhengrong Isle; the armies descended and struck, routing them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan regrouped in Jing and Ying, raised a fleet and twenty thousand men, and fled downriver from Jiangling with the emperor. At Zhengrong Isle Liu Yi's forces fell on him and broke his army completely.

sentences.zh: [16]玄棄眾，復挾天子還復江陵。

translations.literal: [16] Xuan abandoned his troops, again took the Son of Heaven with him, and returned once more to Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: [16] Xuan abandoned his army and fled back to Jiangling again with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 玄黨殷仲文奉晉二皇后還京師。

translations.literal: Xuan's partisan Yin Zhongwen escorted the two empresses of Jin back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's ally Yin Zhongwen sent the two Jin empresses back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 玄至江陵，因西走。

translations.literal: When Xuan reached Jiangling, he then fled west.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Jiangling, Xuan fled west.

sentences.zh: 南郡太守王騰之、荊州別駕王康產奉天子入南郡府。

translations.literal: Administrator of Nan Commandery Wang Tengzhi and Assistant Administrator of Jing Province Wang Kangchan received the Son of Heaven into the Nan Commandery headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Nan Commandery Administrator Wang Tengzhi and Jingzhou Assistant Wang Kangchan lodged the emperor in the commandery seat.

sentences.zh: 初征虜將軍、益州刺史毛璩，遣從孫祐之與參軍費恬送弟喪下，有眾二百。

translations.literal: Initially General Who Conquers the Barbarians and Inspector of Yi Province Mao Jin had sent his younger brother's grandson Youzhi with Staff Officer Fei Tian to escort his younger brother's coffin downstream; they had two hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Mao Jin of Yi Province had sent his grand-nephew Youzhi and staff officer Fei Tian with two hundred men to escort a brother's coffin downstream.

sentences.zh: 璩弟子脩之時為玄屯騎校尉，[17]誘玄以入蜀。

translations.literal: Jin's nephew Xiuzhi at the time was Xuan's Colonel of Escort Cavalry, [17] and enticed Xuan to enter Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's nephew Xiuzhi, then Xuan's Colonel of Escort Cavalry, [17] lured Xuan toward Shu.

sentences.zh: 至枚回洲，恬與祐之迎射之。

translations.literal: When they reached Meihui Isle, Tian and Youzhi met them and shot at them.
translations.idiomatic: At Meihui Isle Fei Tian and Youzhi ambushed and shot at them.

sentences.zh: 益州督護馮遷斬玄首，傳京師。

translations.literal: Yi Province Supervisor Feng Qian beheaded Xuan and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Province Supervisor Feng Qian cut off Xuan's head and sent it to the capital.

sentences.zh: 又斬玄子昇於江陵市。

translations.literal: They also beheaded Xuan's son Sheng in the Jiangling market.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's son Sheng was also beheaded in the Jiangling market.

sentences.zh: 初玄敗於崢嶸洲，義軍以為大事已定，追躡不速。

translations.literal: Initially when Xuan was defeated at Zhengrong Isle, the righteous army thought the great affair was already settled and did not pursue swiftly.
translations.idiomatic: After Xuan's defeat at Zhengrong Isle the righteous army assumed the war was won and did not press the pursuit.

sentences.zh: 玄死幾一旬，眾軍猶不至。

translations.literal: Xuan had been dead nearly ten days before the armies still had not arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Nearly ten days after Xuan's death the main forces had still not arrived.

sentences.zh: 玄從子振逃於華容之涌中，[18]招聚逆黨數千人，晨襲江陵城，居民競出赴之。

translations.literal: Xuan's nephew's son Zhen escaped to the marshes of Huarong, [18] gathered several thousand rebel partisans, and at dawn raided Jiangling city; the residents rushed out to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's grand-nephew Zhen hid in the Huarong marshes, [18] rallied several thousand rebels, and at dawn stormed Jiangling; townspeople rushed out to join him.

sentences.zh: 騰之、康產皆被殺。

translations.literal: Tengzhi and Kangchan were both killed.
translations.idiomatic: Tengzhi and Kangchan were both killed.

sentences.zh: 桓謙先匿於沮川，亦聚眾以應。

translations.literal: Huan Qian had first hidden in Juchuan and also gathered masses to respond.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Qian, hiding in Juchuan, also raised troops in support.

sentences.zh: 振為玄舉哀，立喪廷。

translations.literal: Zhen held mourning for Xuan and established a mourning hall.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen mourned Xuan and set up a mourning hall.

sentences.zh: 謙率眾官奉璽綬于安帝。

translations.literal: Qian led the officials to present the seal and cord to Emperor An.
translations.idiomatic: Qian led the officials in presenting the seal and cord to Emperor An.

sentences.zh: 無忌、道規既至江陵，與桓振戰于靈溪。

translations.literal: Wuji and Daogui, having reached Jiangling, fought Huan Zhen at Ling Stream.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuji and Daogui reached Jiangling they fought Huan Zhen at Ling Stream.

sentences.zh: 玄黨馮該又設伏于楊林，義軍奔敗，退還尋陽。

translations.literal: Xuan's partisan Feng Gai also set an ambush at Yanglin; the righteous army was routed in flight and retreated to Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's ally Feng Gai ambushed them at Yanglin; the righteous army broke and fell back to Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 兗州刺史辛禺懷貳。

translations.literal: Inspector of Yan Province Xin Yu harbored divided loyalties.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou Inspector Xin Yu wavered in loyalty.

sentences.zh: 會北青州刺史劉該反，禺求征該，次淮陰，又反。

translations.literal: It happened that Inspector of Northern Qing Province Liu Gai rebelled; Yu requested to campaign against Gai, halted at Huaiyin, and rebelled again.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qingzhou Inspector Liu Gai rebelled, Yu asked to suppress him, halted at Huaiyin, and rebelled in turn.

sentences.zh: 禺長史羊穆之斬禺，傳首京師。

translations.literal: Yu's Chief Clerk Yang Muzhi beheaded Yu and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's chief clerk Yang Muzhi killed him and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 十月，高祖領青州刺史。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, Gaozu additionally held the post of Inspector of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Gaozu was additionally made Inspector of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 甲仗百人入殿。

translations.literal: A hundred armored men entered the palace hall.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred armored guards entered the palace hall.

sentences.zh: 劉毅諸軍復進至夏口。

translations.literal: Liu Yi's armies again advanced to Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi's forces advanced again to Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 毅攻魯城，道規攻偃月壘，皆拔之。

translations.literal: Yi attacked Lucheng; Daogui attacked Yanyue Fortress; both were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Yi took Lucheng and Daogui took Yanyue Fortress.

sentences.zh: 十二月，諸軍進平巴陵。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the armies advanced and pacified Baling.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the armies pacified Baling.

sentences.zh: 義熙元年正月，毅等至江津，破桓謙、桓振，江陵平，天子反正。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Yixi, Yi and the others reached Jiangjin, defeated Huan Qian and Huan Zhen, pacified Jiangling, and the Son of Heaven returned to right rule.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Yixi 1, Yi reached Jiangjin, defeated Qian and Zhen, pacified Jiangling, and restored the emperor.

sentences.zh: 三月，天子至自江陵。

translations.literal: In the third month the Son of Heaven returned from Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the emperor returned from Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：

translations.literal: An edict said:
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared:

sentences.zh: 古稱大者天地，其次君臣，所以列貫三辰，神人代序，諒理本於造昧，而運周於萬葉。

translations.literal: The ancients said the greatest are Heaven and Earth, next sovereign and minister; thus they rank with the three luminaries, spirits and men succeed one another in order—surely principle originates in primordial obscurity, yet fortune cycles through myriad ages.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients ranked Heaven and Earth first and sovereign and minister next, setting the order of the three luminaries as spirits and men passed the age from darkness into light.

sentences.zh: 故盈否時襲，四靈通其變，王道或昧，貞賢拯其危，天命所以永固，人心所以攸穆。

translations.literal: Hence fullness and denial come in seasons; the four numina communicate their changes; when the kingly way is obscured, the steadfast sage rescues its peril—thus the Mandate of Heaven is forever firm and the hearts of men thereby tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne falters, sages arise to save it; thus the Mandate endures and hearts find peace.

sentences.zh: 雖夏、周中傾，賴靡、申之績，莽、倫載竊，實二代是維。

translations.literal: Although Xia and Zhou midway tottered, they relied on the achievements of Mi and Shen; Wang Mang and Wang Lun for a time usurped, yet in truth the two dynasties were preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Xia and Zhou tottered yet were saved by loyal ministers; usurpers like Wang Mang held power briefly, yet those dynasties survived.

sentences.zh: 或乘資藉號，或業隆異世，猶詩書以之休詠，記策用為美談。

translations.literal: Some seized opportunity to take titles, some their enterprise flourished in another age—still the Odes and Documents praise them, records and annals make them fine tales.
translations.idiomatic: Some seized the moment, some built greatness in another age—poetry and history still praise them.

sentences.zh: 未有因心撫民，而誠發理應，援神器於已淪，若在今之盛者也。

translations.literal: Never before has one, from the heart comforting the people, with sincerity arising in accord with principle, rescued the sacred vessel already sunk, as in the splendor of today.
translations.idiomatic: Never before has a man, moved by pure loyalty, snatched the fallen throne back as in this age.

sentences.zh: 朕以寡昧，遭家不造，越自遘閔，屬當屯極。

translations.literal: We, being few and dim, encountered an ill-formed house; crossing into affliction, we met the time of utmost difficulty.
