translations.idiomatic: We are untested and have suffered a ruined house; misfortune has brought us to the brink.

sentences.zh: 逆臣桓玄，乘釁縱慝，窮凶恣虐，滔天猾夏。

translations.literal: The rebel minister Huan Xuan seized the opportunity and indulged wickedness, to the utmost cruel and tyrannical, flooding heaven with villainy.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Huan Xuan seized his chance, ran riot in cruelty, and flooded the realm with wickedness.

sentences.zh: 遂誣罔人神，肆其篡亂。

translations.literal: He then deceived gods and men and indulged his usurpation and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: He deceived heaven and earth and seized the throne by force.

sentences.zh: 祖宗之基既湮，七廟之饗胥殄，若墜淵谷，未足斯譬。

translations.literal: The foundation of the ancestors was already submerged; the offerings of the seven temples were all extinguished—as if falling into abyss and ravine, not enough for comparison.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral foundation was drowned and the seven temples destroyed—a fall beyond comparison.

sentences.zh: 皇度有晉，天縱英哲，使持節、都督揚徐兗豫青冀幽并江九州諸軍事、鎮軍將軍、徐青二州刺史，忠誠天亮，神武命世，用能貞明協契，義夫響臻。

translations.literal: Fortune had Jin; Heaven endowed it with heroic wisdom: Bearer of the Staff, Commander-in-Chief of the Nine Provinces of Yang, Xu, Yan, Yu, Qing, Ji, You, Bing, and Jiang, General Who Guards the Army, Inspector of Xu and Qing Provinces—loyalty bright as heaven, martial spirit commanding the age—thus able to uphold bright accord and covenant; righteous men responded in gathering.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven blessed Jin with Gaozu—Bearer of the Staff, commander of nine provinces, loyal as daylight and martial as fate itself—so that righteous men rallied to his covenant.

sentences.zh: 故順聲一唱，二溟卷波，英風振路，宸居清翳。

translations.literal: Thus at one call the two seas rolled in waves; heroic wind shook the road; the imperial residence was cleared of obscurity.
translations.idiomatic: At his first summons the realm surged like the two seas; heroic winds swept the roads and the palace was cleared of shadow.

sentences.zh: 暨冠軍將軍毅、輔國將軍無忌、振武將軍道規，舟旗遄邁，而元凶傳首，回戈疊揮，則荊、漢霧廓。

translations.literal: Then Champion-General Yi, General Who Assists the State Wuji, and General Who Quells Might Daogui—ships and banners sped forward; the arch-rebel's head was transmitted; turning spears again and again, then Jing and Han were cleared of mist.
translations.idiomatic: Then Yi, Wuji, and Daogui raced downriver; the chief rebel's head was sent home; turning their spears again, Jing and Han were cleared of mist.

sentences.zh: 俾宣、元之祚，永固於嵩、岱，傾基重造，再集於朕躬。

translations.literal: Thus the fortunes of Xuan and Yuan were forever fixed on Song and Dai; the overturned foundation was heavily rebuilt and again gathered upon Our person.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Jin's fortune was rebuilt on Song and Dai, and the fallen throne was raised again upon us.

sentences.zh: 宗廟歆七百之祜，皇基融載新之命。

translations.literal: The ancestral temples enjoyed seven hundred years of blessing; the imperial foundation melted and bore the new Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral temples received blessing once more; the throne received a renewed Mandate.

sentences.zh: 念功惟德，永言銘懷。

translations.literal: Considering merit, only virtue; forever inscribed in remembrance.
translations.idiomatic: Merit calls for remembrance; we inscribe it forever.

sentences.zh: 固已道冠開闢，獨絕終古，書契以來，未之前聞矣。

translations.literal: Already his Way crowns the founding age, alone unmatched through antiquity; since the age of writing, none has been heard of before.
translations.idiomatic: His achievement crowns the age and has no parallel since records began.

sentences.zh: 雖則功高靡尚，理至難文，而崇庸命德，哲王攸先者，將以弘道制治，深關盛衰。

translations.literal: Although merit is high beyond compare and principle reaches what words cannot reach, yet honoring merit and appointing by virtue—wise kings put these first—in order to expand the Way, regulate governance, and deeply bind flourishing and decline.
translations.idiomatic: Though his merit exceeds words, wise kings honor merit to bind the realm's rise and fall to the Way.

sentences.zh: 故伊、望膺殊命之錫，桓、文饗備物之禮，況宏徵不世，顧邈百代者，宜極名器之隆，以光大國之盛。

translations.literal: Thus Yi and Wang received extraordinary appointments; Huan and Wen enjoyed rites of full provision; how much more when the great summons is not of the age and looks across a hundred generations—one should reach the utmost of titles and honors to magnify the state's splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and Wang received extraordinary honors; Huan and Wen received full rites—how much more should this unmatched service be crowned with the highest titles?

sentences.zh: 而鎮軍謙虛自衷，誠旨屢顯，朕重逆仲父，乃所以愈彰德美也。

translations.literal: Yet the General Who Guards the Army is modest from the heart; sincere intent has repeatedly appeared; We, heavily going against the uncle-father, thereby only make the virtue and beauty more manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the General Who Guards the Army is humble at heart; the more we press him, the brighter his virtue shines.

sentences.zh: 鎮軍可進位侍中、車騎將軍、都督中外諸軍事，使持節、徐、青二州刺史如故。

translations.literal: The General Who Guards the Army may advance to Palace Attendant, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Commander-in-Chief of All Military Affairs Within and Without, Bearer of the Staff, Inspector of Xu and Qing Provinces as before.
translations.idiomatic: The General Who Guards the Army is promoted to Palace Attendant, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Commander-in-Chief of all armies at home and abroad, with Xu and Qing as before.

sentences.zh: 顯祚大邦，啟茲疆宇。

translations.literal: Manifest fortune in a great state; open this territory.
translations.idiomatic: Let great fortune shine upon the state and open this domain.

sentences.zh: 高祖固讓。

translations.literal: Gaozu firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu refused.

sentences.zh: 加錄尚書事，又不受，屢請歸藩。

translations.literal: He was additionally made Recorder of the Masters of Writing, again did not accept, and repeatedly requested to return to his fief.
translations.idiomatic: He was also offered the post of Recorder of the Masters of Writing, refused again, and repeatedly asked to return to his command.

sentences.zh: 天子不許，遣百僚敦勸，又親幸公第。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven did not permit it; he sent the hundred officials to press him earnestly, and also personally visited the Duke's residence.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not hear of it, sent officials to urge him, and visited his residence in person.

sentences.zh: 高祖惶懼詣闕陳請，天子不能奪。

translations.literal: Gaozu, fearful and alarmed, went to the palace gate to state his plea; the Son of Heaven could not override him.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu went to court in apparent alarm to plead his case, and the emperor could not refuse him.

sentences.zh: 是月，旋鎮丹徒。

translations.literal: That month he returned to garrison Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: That month he returned to garrison Dantu.

sentences.zh: 天子重遣大使敦勸，又不受。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven again sent a grand envoy to press him earnestly; again he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a high envoy to urge him again; again he refused.

sentences.zh: 乃改授都督荊、司、梁、益、寧、雍、涼七州，并前十六州諸軍事，本官如故。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was reassigned as Commander-in-Chief of the Military Affairs of the Seven Provinces of Jing, Si, Liang, Yi, Ning, Yong, and Liang, together with the previous sixteen provinces, his original offices remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was then given command of seven more provinces in addition to his existing sixteen, with his other titles unchanged.

sentences.zh: 於是受命解青州，加領兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon upon accepting the appointment he relinquished Qing Province and was additionally made Inspector of Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: On accepting, he gave up Qing Province and took Yan Province as well.

sentences.zh: 盧循浮海破廣州，獲刺史吳隱之。

translations.literal: Lu Xun crossed the sea, captured Guangzhou, and took Inspector Wu Yinzhi prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun sailed from the sea, seized Guangzhou, and captured Inspector Wu Yinzhi.

sentences.zh: 即以循為廣州刺史，以其同黨徐道覆為始興相。

translations.literal: He thereupon made Xun Inspector of Guang Province and his fellow partisan Xu Daofu Administrator of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was made Inspector of Guang Province and his ally Xu Daofu was made Administrator of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，督交、廣二州。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year, he was made Supervisor of Jiao and Guang Provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of year two he was made Supervisor of Jiao and Guang Provinces.

sentences.zh: 十月，高祖上言曰：「昔天禍皇室，巨狡縱篡，臣等義惟舊隸，豫蒙國恩，仰契信順之符，俯厲人臣之憤，雖社稷之靈，抑亦事由眾濟。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Gaozu submitted a memorial saying: "Formerly Heaven afflicted the imperial house; the great villain indulged usurpation. We, your ministers, by righteousness were old retainers and beforehand received the state's grace; looking up we matched the sign of faith and obedience, looking down we sharpened the indignation of subjects—though the altars of state had their spirits, yet the affair also succeeded through the multitude's aid.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Gaozu memorialized: "When Heaven struck the throne and the great usurper ran wild, we old servants of Jin rose in righteous anger. Though the altars had their spirits, victory came only through many hands.

sentences.zh: 其翼獎忠懃之佐，文武畢力之士，敷執在己之謙，用虧國體之大。

translations.literal: In rewarding and encouraging loyal and diligent assistants and civil and military men who exerted all strength, I repeatedly held to personal modesty and thereby diminished the great body of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in rewarding the loyal I kept too much modesty for myself and slighted the dignity of the state.

sentences.zh: 輒申攝眾軍先上，[19]同謀起義，始平京口、廣陵二城，臣及撫軍將軍毅等二百七十二人，并後赴義出都緣道大戰，所餘一千五百六十六人，又輔國將軍長民、故給事中王元德等十人，合一千八百四十八人，乞正封賞。

translations.literal: I have therefore reported first on behalf of the assembled armies, [19] those who together plotted the uprising: first pacifying the two cities of Jingkou and Guangling—myself and General Who Pacifies the Army Yi and two hundred seventy-two others—and those who afterward joined the righteous cause leaving the capital and fighting along the route, the remaining one thousand five hundred sixty-six; also General Who Assists the State Changmin and the late Palace Attendant Wang Yuande and ten others—in all one thousand eight hundred forty-eight—requesting proper enfeoffment and reward.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore submit first, [19] on behalf of the armies that plotted the uprising: the two hundred seventy-two of us who first took Jingkou and Guangling, the one thousand five hundred sixty-six who fought along the road, and ten others including Changmin and the late Wang Yuande—one thousand eight hundred forty-eight in all—seeking proper rewards."

sentences.zh: 其西征眾軍，須論集續上。

translations.literal: The western campaign armies must be discussed and reported in a follow-up memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The western campaign forces will be listed in a later memorial.

sentences.zh: 」於是尚書奏封唱義謀主鎮軍將軍裕豫章郡公，食邑萬戶，賜絹三萬匹。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the Masters of Writing memorialized enfeoffing the chief plotter of the righteous uprising, General Who Guards the Army Yu, as Duke of Yuzhang with ten thousand households and a fief, granting thirty thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing then enfeoffed Gaozu, chief of the righteous plot, as Duke of Yuzhang with ten thousand households and thirty thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 其餘封賞各有差。

translations.literal: The rest received enfeoffments and rewards each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: The rest were rewarded according to rank.

sentences.zh: 鎮軍府佐吏，降故太傅謝安府一等。

translations.literal: Staff officers of the General Who Guards the Army's headquarters were reduced one grade from those of the late Grand Tutor Xie An's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Staff at Gaozu's headquarters were ranked one grade below those of the late Grand Tutor Xie An.

sentences.zh: 十一月，天子重申前令，加高祖侍中，進號車騎將軍、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the Son of Heaven again reiterated the previous order, adding Gaozu as Palace Attendant and advancing his title to General of Chariots and Cavalry with the Honorific Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the emperor again offered him Palace Attendant, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and honors equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 固讓。

translations.literal: He firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He refused.

sentences.zh: 詔遣百僚敦勸。

translations.literal: An edict sent the hundred officials to press him earnestly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the officials to urge him again.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，高祖還京師，將詣廷尉，天子先詔獄官不得受，詣闕陳讓，乃見聽。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year Gaozu returned to the capital and was about to go to the Court of Justice; the Son of Heaven first edicted that prison officials were not to receive him; he went to the palace gate to state his refusal and was then permitted to leave.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year three Gaozu returned to the capital, tried to surrender himself to the Court of Justice, was turned away by imperial order, pleaded at the gate, and was allowed to go.

sentences.zh: 旋于丹徒。

translations.literal: He then returned to Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: He then returned to Dantu.

sentences.zh: 閏月，府將駱冰謀作亂，將被執，單騎走，追斬之。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month headquarters officer Luo Bing plotted rebellion; about to be seized, he fled alone on horseback; they pursued and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month staff officer Luo Bing plotted revolt; caught and fleeing alone on horseback, he was run down and killed.

sentences.zh: 誅冰父永嘉太守球。

translations.literal: Bing's father, Administrator of Yongjia Qiu, was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Bing's father Qiu, Administrator of Yongjia, was executed.

sentences.zh: 球本東陽郡史，孫恩之亂，起義於長山，故見擢用。

translations.literal: Qiu had originally been a clerk of Dongyang Commandery; in Sun En's rebellion he had risen in righteousness at Changshan and therefore was promoted and employed.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu had been a Dongyang clerk who rose against Sun En at Changshan and was promoted for it.

sentences.zh: 初桓玄之敗，以桓冲忠貞，署其孫胤。

translations.literal: Initially when Huan Xuan was defeated, because Huan Chong had been loyal and steadfast, he appointed Chong's grandson Yin.
translations.idiomatic: After Huan Xuan's first defeat he had appointed Chong's grandson Yin for the Huan clan's loyalty.

sentences.zh: 至是冰謀以胤為主，與東陽太守殷仲文潛相連結。

translations.literal: At this time Bing's plot was to make Yin the leader, secretly linking with Administrator of Dongyang Yin Zhongwen.
translations.idiomatic: Bing now plotted to make Yin their figurehead and secretly linked with Dongyang Administrator Yin Zhongwen.

sentences.zh: 乃誅仲文及仲文二弟。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhongwen and Zhongwen's two younger brothers were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen and his two brothers were executed.

sentences.zh: 凡桓玄餘黨，至是皆誅夷。

translations.literal: All remaining partisans of Huan Xuan were at this time exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Every remaining Huan Xuan partisan was now wiped out.

sentences.zh: 天子遣兼太常葛籍授公策曰：「有扈滔天，夷羿乘釁，亂節干紀，實橈皇極。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven sent Acting Minister of Ceremonies Ge Ji to confer upon the Duke a patent saying: "Youhu flooded heaven; Yi of Xia seized the opportunity; disorderly conduct violated the seasons and in truth overturned the imperial pinnacle.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Acting Minister of Ceremonies Ge Ji with a patent of investiture: "Rebellion flooded heaven as Yi of Xia once did; the usurper overturned the throne itself.

sentences.zh: 賊臣桓玄，怙寵肆逆，乃摧傾華、霍，倒拔嵩、岱，五嶽既夷，六地易所。

translations.literal: The villainous minister Huan Xuan, relying on favor and indulging rebellion, then overthrew Hua and Huo, uprooted Song and Dai; the five peaks were already leveled, the six lands changed their place.
translations.idiomatic: The traitor Huan Xuan, drunk on favor, toppled pillars like Hua and Huo and uprooted mountains like Song and Dai.

sentences.zh: 公命世英縱，藏器待時，因心資敬，誓雪國恥，慨憤陵夷，誠發宵寐。

translations.literal: The Duke, commanding the age by heroic talent, stored capacity awaiting the time; by the heart he drew on reverence, swore to wipe away the state's shame, indignant at decline, sincerity issued from sleepless nights.
translations.idiomatic: You, hero of the age, waited your moment, swore to wipe away national shame, and burned with sleepless loyalty.

sentences.zh: 既而歲月屢遷，神器已遠，忠孝幽寄，實貫三靈。

translations.literal: Then years repeatedly passed; the sacred vessel was already distant; loyalty and filial piety were lodged in obscurity—in truth penetrating the three numina.
translations.idiomatic: Years passed and the throne seemed lost, yet your loyalty reached heaven, earth, and the spirits.

sentences.zh: 爾乃介石勝機，宣契畢舉，訴蒼天以為正，揮義旅而一驅。

translations.literal: Thereupon like a steadfast stone at the winning moment, you declared the covenant and completed the undertaking, appealed to azure Heaven as the standard, and swept the righteous host in one drive.
translations.idiomatic: Then, firm as stone at the decisive hour, you raised the righteous host under Heaven's judgment and swept forward as one.

sentences.zh: 奔鋒數百，勢烈激電，百萬不能抗限，制路日直植城。

translations.literal: Rushing spears numbered in the hundreds; momentum was fierce as lightning; a million could not resist the limit; controlling the road, day by day they planted cities.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds of spears charged like lightning; no army could stand before you; city after city fell to your march.

sentences.zh: [20]遂使衝鯨潰流，暴鱗江漢，廟勝遠加，重氛載滌，二儀廓清，三光反照，事遂永代，功高開闢，理微稱謂，義感朕心。

translations.literal: [20] Thus he made rushing whales break their flow, exposed scales on the Jiang and Han; victory from afar was added, heavy miasma was again washed away; the two principles were cleared, the three luminaries reflected again; the affair will endure for generations, merit towers over the founding age—principle subtle, title fitting; righteousness moved Our heart.
translations.idiomatic: [20] Whales broke in the rivers, the Jiang and Han were cleared, heaven and earth brightened, and the three luminaries shone again—merit beyond founding, righteousness that moved our heart.

sentences.zh: 若夫道為身濟，猶縻厥爵，況乃誠德俱深，勳冠天人者乎。

translations.literal: If the Way for the person is still to be rewarded with rank, how much more when sincerity and virtue are both deep and merit crowns heaven and man.
translations.idiomatic: If even personal service earns rank, how much more merit that crowns heaven and earth?

sentences.zh: 是用建茲邦國，永祚山河，言念載懷，匪云足報。

translations.literal: Therefore We establish this state, forever endow these mountains and rivers; speaking of it fills the heart—it is not enough for repayment.
translations.idiomatic: We therefore establish this domain and endow these mountains and rivers, knowing no reward can suffice.

sentences.zh: 往欽哉！

translations.literal: Go—revere it!
translations.idiomatic: Go, and revere it!

sentences.zh: 俾屏余一人，長弼皇晉，流風垂祚，暉烈無窮。

translations.literal: Make yourself a screen for Us alone, long aid august Jin; flowing wind and enduring fortune, brilliant splendor without end.
translations.idiomatic: Be our shield, long support great Jin, and let your glory endure without end.

sentences.zh: 其降承嘉策，對敭朕命。」

translations.literal: Descend and receive this fine patent; respond and proclaim Our command."
translations.idiomatic: Receive this patent and proclaim our command."

sentences.zh: 十二月，司徒、錄尚書、揚州刺史王謐薨。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Regent, Recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Inspector of Yang Province Wang Mi died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Regent Wang Mi died.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，徵公入輔，授侍中、車騎將軍、開府儀同三司、揚州刺史、錄尚書，徐兗二州刺史如故。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year the Duke was summoned to assist at court and was appointed Palace Attendant, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Honorific Equal to the Three Excellencies, Inspector of Yang Province, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing; Inspector of Xu and Yan Provinces remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year four he was summoned to court as Palace Attendant, General of Chariots and Cavalry, Inspector of Yang Province, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing, retaining Xu and Yan.

sentences.zh: 表解兗州。

translations.literal: He memorialized to relinquish Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to give up Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 先是遣冠軍劉敬宣伐蜀賊譙縱，無功而返。

translations.literal: Earlier Champion-General Liu Jingxuan had been sent to campaign against the Shu bandit Qiao Zong and returned without achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liu Jingxuan had been sent against the Shu rebel Qiao Zong and returned empty-handed.

sentences.zh: 九月，以敬宣挫退，遜位，不許。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, because Jingxuan had been defeated and retreated, he yielded his position; it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Jingxuan offered to step down after his defeat; the offer was refused.

sentences.zh: 乃降為中軍將軍，開府如故。

translations.literal: He was then reduced to General of the Central Army, his headquarters honorific remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to General of the Central Army while keeping his headquarters honors.

sentences.zh: 初偽燕王鮮卑慕容德僭號於青州，德死，兄子超襲位，前後屢為邊患。

translations.literal: Initially the false Yan King, the Xianbei Murong De, had usurped title in Qing Province; when De died, his elder brother's son Chao succeeded him; before and after he repeatedly became a border affliction.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei pretender Murong De had seized Qing Province; after his death his nephew Chao succeeded him and raided the borders repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 五年二月，大掠淮北，執陽平太守劉千載、濟南太守趙元，驅略千餘家。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year he greatly plundered north of the Huai, seized Administrator of Yangping Liu Qianzai and Administrator of Jinan Zhao Yuan, and drove off more than a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year five Chao ravaged north of the Huai, seized two administrators, and carried off more than a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 三月，公抗表北討，以丹陽尹孟昶監中軍留府事。

translations.literal: In the third month the Duke submitted a memorial resisting and campaigning north; he made Administrator of Danyang Meng Chang supervise the central army and remain to manage headquarters affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Gaozu memorialized for a northern campaign and left Meng Chang to supervise headquarters.

sentences.zh: 四月，舟師發京都，泝淮入泗。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the fleet departed the capital, went upstream on the Huai into the Si.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the fleet left the capital and sailed up the Huai into the Si.

sentences.zh: 五月，至下邳，留船艦輜重，步軍進琅邪。

translations.literal: In the fifth month they reached Xiapi, left ships and baggage, and the infantry advanced to Langya.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month they reached Xiapi, left the ships and supplies, and marched into Langya.

sentences.zh: 所過皆築城留守。

translations.literal: Wherever they passed they built fortresses and left garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Every place they passed they fortified and garrisoned.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑梁父、莒城二戍並奔走。

translations.literal: The Xianbei garrisons of Liangfu and Jucheng both fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei garrisons at Liangfu and Jucheng both fled.

sentences.zh: 慕容超聞王師將至，其大將公孫五樓說超：「宜斷據大峴，刈除粟苗，堅壁清野以待之。

translations.literal: When Murong Chao heard the royal army was about to arrive, his great general Gongsun Wulou advised Chao: "You should hold and block the Great Pass, cut the grain seedlings, and empty the countryside to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the imperial army was coming, Chao's general Gongsun Wulou advised: "Hold the Great Pass, cut the grain, and strip the countryside to wait them out.

sentences.zh: 彼僑軍無資，求戰不得，旬月之間，折棰以笞之耳。

translations.literal: Their expeditionary army has no supplies; unable to obtain battle, within ten days and a month you can break them with a whip.
translations.idiomatic: Without supplies they cannot fight; in a month you can beat them with a whip."

sentences.zh: 」超不從，曰：「彼遠來疲勞，勢不能久，但當引令過峴，我以鐵騎踐之，不憂不破也。

translations.literal: " Chao did not follow, saying: "They come from afar weary; their momentum cannot last long—only lead them to pass the pass; I with iron cavalry will tread them down; no worry of not breaking them.
translations.idiomatic: Chao refused: "They are tired from afar and cannot last. Let them through the pass and my iron cavalry will crush them.

sentences.zh: 豈有預芟苗稼，先自䠞弱邪。

translations.literal: How could one beforehand cut grain seedlings and first weaken oneself?
translations.idiomatic: Why cut our own grain and weaken ourselves first?"

sentences.zh: 」初公將行，議者以為賊聞大軍遠出，必不敢戰，若不斷大峴，當堅守廣固，刈粟清野，以絕三軍之資，非唯難以有功，將不能自反。

translations.literal: " Initially when the Duke was about to march, those who discussed the matter thought the bandits, hearing the great army had gone far out, would surely not dare fight; if they did not block the Great Pass, they would surely hold Guanggu firmly, cut grain and empty the countryside to cut off the three armies' supplies—not only would it be hard to achieve merit, they would also be unable to return.
translations.idiomatic: Before the march, critics warned that if the Xianbei did not fight at the pass they would hold Guanggu, strip the land, and starve the army—not only failing to win but risking no return.

sentences.zh: 公曰：「我揣之熟矣。

translations.literal: The Duke said: "I have calculated it thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said: "I have weighed this carefully.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑貪，[21]不及遠計，進利剋獲，退惜粟苗。

translations.literal: The Xianbei are greedy, [21] unable to plan far; advancing they covet gain, retreating they cherish grain seedlings.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei are greedy, [21] short-sighted; advancing they want loot, retreating they cling to their grain.

sentences.zh: 謂我孤軍遠入，不能持久，不過進據臨朐，退守廣固。

translations.literal: They think my lone army has entered far and cannot endure long—nothing more than advancing to occupy Linqu and retreating to hold Guanggu.
translations.idiomatic: They will think our lone army cannot endure and will only advance to Linqu or fall back to Guanggu.

sentences.zh: 我一得入峴，則人無退心，驅必死之眾，向懷貳之虜，何憂不剋。

translations.literal: Once I enter the pass, then men will have no heart to retreat; driving troops resolved to die against bandits with divided hearts—what worry of not conquering?
translations.idiomatic: Once we are through the pass, my men will not retreat; driving desperate soldiers against wavering foes, how can we fail?

sentences.zh: 彼不能清野固守，為諸君保之。

translations.literal: They cannot empty the countryside and hold firm—I guarantee that for you all.
translations.idiomatic: They will not strip the land and stand firm—I guarantee it."

sentences.zh: 」公既入峴，舉手指天曰：「吾事濟矣！」

translations.literal: " After the Duke had entered the pass, he raised his hand and pointed to heaven, saying: "My affair is accomplished!"
translations.idiomatic: Passing through the Great Pass, Gaozu pointed to heaven and cried: "It is done!"

sentences.zh: 六月，慕容超遣五樓及廣寧王賀賴盧先據臨朐城。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Murong Chao sent Wulou and Prince of Guangning Helailu to first occupy Linqu city.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Chao sent Wulou and Prince of Guangning Helailu to hold Linqu.

sentences.zh: 既聞大軍至，留羸老守廣固，乃悉出。

translations.literal: Having heard the great army had arrived, he left the weak and old to hold Guanggu and then came out with his full force.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the main army had arrived, he left the weak to hold Guanggu and came out in full strength.

sentences.zh: 臨朐有巨蔑水，去城四十里。

translations.literal: At Linqu there was the Jumie River, forty li from the city.
translations.idiomatic: Linqu had the Jumie River forty li from the city.

sentences.zh: 超告五樓曰：「急往據之，晉軍得水，則難擊也。

translations.literal: Chao told Wulou: "Hurry and go hold it; if the Jin army gets water, then it will be hard to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: Chao told Wulou: "Seize the river at once; if Jin gets water, they will be hard to attack."

sentences.zh: 」五樓馳進。

translations.literal: " Wulou galloped forward.
translations.idiomatic: Wulou raced ahead.

sentences.zh: 龍驤將軍孟龍符領騎居前，奔往爭之，五樓乃退。

translations.literal: General of the Dragon Cavalry Meng Longfu led cavalry in the van, galloping to contend for it; Wulou then retreated.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Longfu's cavalry charged for the river and Wulou fell back.

sentences.zh: 眾軍步進，有車四千兩，分車為兩翼，方軌徐行，車悉張幔，御者執矟。

translations.literal: The mass army advanced on foot; there were four thousand carts; they divided the carts into two wings, marching in square file at a steady pace; all carts were draped with curtains; drivers held spears.
translations.idiomatic: The infantry advanced with four thousand carts in two wings, curtains drawn, drivers armed with spears.

sentences.zh: 又以輕騎為遊軍。

translations.literal: They also used light cavalry as roaming troops.
translations.idiomatic: Light cavalry screened the march.

sentences.zh: 軍令嚴肅，行伍齊整。

translations.literal: Military orders were strict; ranks and files were orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Discipline was iron; the columns were perfect.

sentences.zh: 未及臨朐數里，賊鐵騎萬餘，前後交至。

translations.literal: Not yet several li from Linqu, more than ten thousand of the bandits' iron cavalry arrived before and behind in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Still miles from Linqu, more than ten thousand Xianbei horsemen struck front and rear.

sentences.zh: 公命兗州刺史劉藩、弟并州刺史道憐、諮議參軍劉敬宣、陶延壽、參軍劉懷玉、慎仲道、索邈等，齊力擊之。

translations.literal: The Duke ordered Inspector of Yan Province Liu Fan, his younger brother Inspector of Bing Province Liu Daolian, Adviser Liu Jingxuan, Tao Yanshou, Staff Officer Liu Huaiyu, Shen Zhongdao, Suo Miao, and others to strike them together with combined strength.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent Liu Fan, Liu Daolian, Liu Jingxuan, Tao Yanshou, Liu Huaiyu, Shen Zhongdao, Suo Miao, and others to meet them together.

sentences.zh: 日向昃，公遣諮議參軍檀韶直趨臨朐。

translations.literal: As the sun approached the west, the Duke sent Adviser Tan Shao to charge straight for Linqu.
translations.idiomatic: Near sunset he sent Tan Shao straight at Linqu.

sentences.zh: 詔率建威將軍向彌、參軍胡藩馳往，即日陷城，斬其牙旗，悉虜超輜重。

translations.literal: The edict led General Who Establishes Might Xiang Mi and Staff Officer Hu Fan to gallop there; that same day they stormed the city, cut down its command pennant, and captured all of Chao's baggage.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Mi and Hu Fan galloped up, took the city that day, cut down its pennant, and seized Chao's baggage train.

sentences.zh: 超聞臨朐已拔，引眾走，公親鼓之，賊乃大奔。

translations.literal: Chao, hearing Linqu had fallen, led his masses in flight; the Duke personally beat the drums; the bandits then fled in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Linqu had fallen, Chao turned to flee; Gaozu beat the drums himself and the enemy broke.

sentences.zh: 超遁還廣固。

translations.literal: Chao escaped back to Guanggu.
translations.idiomatic: Chao fled back to Guanggu.

sentences.zh: 獲超馬、偽輦、玉璽、豹尾等，送于京師。

translations.literal: They captured Chao's horses, false imperial carriage, jade seal, leopard-tail insignia, and the like, and sent them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: They captured Chao's horses, false regalia, jade seal, and leopard-tail banners and sent them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 斬其大將段暉等十餘人，其餘斬獲千計。

translations.literal: They beheaded his great general Duan Hui and more than ten others; the rest killed and captured numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: They killed General Duan Hui and more than ten others; thousands more were slain or taken.

sentences.zh: 明日，大軍進廣固，即屠大城，超退保小城。

translations.literal: The next day the great army advanced on Guanggu, immediately slaughtered the outer city, and Chao retreated to hold the inner city.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they reached Guanggu, stormed the outer city, and Chao withdrew into the inner citadel.

sentences.zh: 於是設長圍守之，圍高三丈，外穿三重塹。

translations.literal: Thereupon they set a long encirclement to besiege it; the encirclement was three zhang high; outside they dug three layers of moat.
translations.idiomatic: They laid a long siege with a three-zhang wall and three rings of moats.

sentences.zh: 停江、淮轉輸，館穀於齊土。

translations.literal: They halted transport from the Jiang and Huai and stored grain in Qi territory.
translations.idiomatic: They cut river supply lines and stored grain locally in Qi.

sentences.zh: 撫納降附，華戎歡悅，援才授爵，因而任之。

translations.literal: They comforted and accepted those who surrendered; Chinese and barbarians rejoiced; selecting talent they granted ranks and thereby employed them.
translations.idiomatic: They welcomed surrendering Chinese and barbarians alike, enlisting talent as they came.

sentences.zh: 七月，詔加公北青、冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh month an edict added the Duke as Inspector of Northern Qing and Ji Provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was additionally made Inspector of Northern Qing and Ji Provinces.

sentences.zh: 超大將垣遵、遵弟苗並率眾歸順。

translations.literal: Chao's great generals Yuan Zun and Zun's younger brother Miao both led their masses to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Chao's generals Yuan Zun and his brother Miao surrendered with their troops.

sentences.zh: 公方治攻具，城上人曰：「汝不得張綱，何能為也。

translations.literal: The Duke was just preparing siege engines when the men on the wall said: "You cannot get Zhang Gang—what can you do?
translations.idiomatic: As Gaozu built siege engines, defenders on the wall taunted: "Without Zhang Gang you can do nothing."

sentences.zh: 」綱者，超偽尚書郎，其人有巧思。

translations.literal: " Gang was Chao's false Masters of Writing Gentleman; this man had ingenious thought.
translations.idiomatic: "Gang" was Chao's engineering officer, a man of clever invention.

sentences.zh: 會超遣綱稱藩於姚興，乞師請救。

translations.literal: It happened that Chao sent Gang to declare himself a vassal to Yao Xing and beg troops for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Chao had sent Gang to Yao Xing to beg for aid.

sentences.zh: 興偽許之，而實憚公，不敢遣。

translations.literal: Xing falsely promised, yet in truth feared the Duke and did not dare send troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing promised falsely but feared Gaozu and sent no troops.

sentences.zh: 綱從長安還，泰山太守申宣執送之。

translations.literal: Gang returned from Chang'an; Administrator of Taishan Shen Xuan seized and sent him under escort.
translations.idiomatic: Returning from Chang'an, Gang was seized by Taishan Administrator Shen Xuan.

sentences.zh: 及升綱於樓車，[22]以示城內，城內莫不失色。

translations.literal: When Gang was raised on the tower cart, [22] to show those inside the city, everyone inside lost color.
translations.idiomatic: Gang was raised on a siege tower, [22] shown to the city, and the defenders went pale.

sentences.zh: 於是使綱大治攻具。

translations.literal: Thereupon they had Gang greatly prepare siege engines.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu then put Gang to work building siege engines.

sentences.zh: 超求救不獲，綱反見虜，轉憂懼。

translations.literal: Chao's plea for rescue was not obtained; Gang in turn was captured; he turned to worry and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Rescue never came; Gang was captured instead; Chao grew desperate.

sentences.zh: 乃請稱藩，求割大峴為界，獻馬千疋。

translations.literal: He then requested to declare himself a vassal, asking to cede the Great Pass as a boundary and present a thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: Chao offered submission, the Great Pass as border, and a thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 不聽，圍之轉急。

translations.literal: They did not listen; the siege grew tighter.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu refused; the siege tightened.

sentences.zh: 河北居民荷戈負糧至者，日以千數。

translations.literal: Residents north of the Yellow River carrying spears and grain who arrived numbered more than a thousand each day.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand northerners a day arrived bearing arms and grain.

sentences.zh: 錄事參軍劉穆之，有經略才具，公以為謀主，動止必諮焉。

translations.literal: Recorder of Affairs Liu Muzhi had talent for strategy and administration; the Duke made him chief planner; in movement and rest he always consulted him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Muzhi, Gaozu's chief strategist, was consulted on every move.

sentences.zh: 時姚興遣使告公云：「慕容見與隣好，又以窮告急，今當遣鐵騎十萬，逕據洛陽。

translations.literal: At that time Yao Xing sent an envoy to tell the Duke: "Murong Chao and I are neighboring friends; again he has in extremity begged for help; now I shall send one hundred thousand iron cavalry to take Luoyang directly.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing sent word: "Chao is my neighbor and begged for help; I will send one hundred thousand horsemen straight to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 晉軍若不退者，便當遣鐵騎長驅而進。

translations.literal: If the Jin army does not withdraw, then I shall send iron cavalry in a long drive forward.
translations.idiomatic: If your army does not withdraw, those horsemen will drive straight onward."

sentences.zh: 」公呼興使答曰：「語汝姚興，我定燕之後，息甲三年，當平關、洛。

translations.literal: Gaozu called to Yao Xing's envoy and replied: "Tell Yao Xing: after I settle Yan I shall rest the armies three years, then pacify Guan and Luo.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu answered the envoy: "Tell Yao Xing that once Yan is settled I will stand the armies down for three years, then take Guanzhong and Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 今能自送，便可速來。

translations.literal: If you can come of your own accord now, then come quickly.
translations.idiomatic: If you mean to come, come now.

sentences.zh: 」穆之聞有羌使，馳入，而公發遣已去。

translations.literal: Muzhi heard a Qiang envoy had arrived, rushed in, but Gaozu had already sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi heard a Qiang envoy had come and hurried in, only to find Gaozu had already dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 以興所言并答，具語穆之。

translations.literal: He reported Yao Xing's words and his own reply in full to Muzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He told Muzhi everything Yao Xing had said and how he had answered.

sentences.zh: 穆之尤公曰：「常日事無大小，必賜與謀之。

translations.literal: Muzhi reproached Gaozu, saying: "On ordinary days, no matter how small the affair, you always consult me.
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi rebuked him: "You consult me on every matter, great or small.

sentences.zh: 此宜善詳之，云何卒爾便答。

translations.literal: This ought to have been considered carefully—why answer so abruptly?
translations.idiomatic: This deserved careful thought. Why answer on the spot?

sentences.zh: 公所答興言，未能威敵，正足怒彼耳。

translations.literal: Your reply to Yao Xing cannot overawe the enemy; it can only enrage him.
translations.idiomatic: Your words will not frighten the enemy—they will only provoke him.

sentences.zh: 若燕未可拔，羌救奄至，不審何以待之？

translations.literal: If Yan cannot yet be taken and Qiang relief arrives suddenly, how do you propose to meet it?"
translations.idiomatic: If Yan is not yet captured and Qiang reinforcements appear, what then?"

sentences.zh: 」公笑曰：「此是兵機，非卿所解，故不語耳。

translations.literal: Gaozu smiled and said: "This is military stratagem—not something you would understand, which is why I did not tell you.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu smiled: "That was military calculation, not something you follow. That is why I did not tell you.

sentences.zh: 夫兵貴神速，彼若審能遣救，必畏我知，寧容先遣信命。

translations.literal: In warfare speed is precious; if he could truly send relief, he would fear that we know and would never first dispatch a message.
translations.idiomatic: Speed is everything in war. If he truly meant to rescue Chao, he would not have sent a messenger first—we would have learned of it too soon.

sentences.zh: 此是其見我伐燕，內已懷懼，自張之辭耳。」

translations.literal: This is because he sees us attacking Yan, is already afraid within, and speaks to puff himself up."
translations.idiomatic: He sees us crushing Yan and is bluffing from fear."

sentences.zh: 九月，進公太尉、中書監，固讓。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Gaozu was promoted to Grand Commandant and Supervisor of the Secretariat; he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was offered Grand Commandant and Supervisor of the Secretariat and refused.

sentences.zh: 偽徐州刺史段宏先奔索虜，十月，自河北歸順。

translations.literal: The false Inspector of Xu Province Duan Hong had first fled to the Northern Wei; in the tenth month he came from north of the Yellow River and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Hong, the Xianbei appointee as Inspector of Xu Province, had fled to the Wei; in the tenth month he returned from north of the river and submitted.

translations.literal: Editorial note twenty-three.
translations.idiomatic: See editorial note twenty-three.

sentences.zh: 張綱治攻具成，設諸奇巧，飛樓木幔之屬，莫不畢備。

translations.literal: Zhang Gang finished preparing siege engines, setting up every ingenious device—flying towers, wooden screens, and the like—nothing was lacking.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gang completed the siege train: flying towers, wooden mantlets, and every clever engine imaginable.

sentences.zh: 城上火石弓矢，無所用之。

translations.literal: Fire stones, bows, and arrows on the walls were of no use.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders' stones, bows, and arrows on the walls availed nothing.

sentences.zh: 六年二月丁亥，屠廣固。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year, on dinghai, Guanggu was sacked.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai in the second month of year six, Guanggu fell and was put to the sword.

sentences.zh: 超踰城走，征虜賊曹喬胥獲之，殺其王公以下，[24]納口萬餘，馬二千疋，送超京師，斬于建康市。

translations.literal: Chao fled over the wall; the bandit-capturing officer Qiao of the Expeditionary Force seized him. Those from princes and ministers downward were killed, [24] more than ten thousand people were taken captive, and two thousand horses; Chao was sent to the capital and executed in the Jiankang market.
translations.idiomatic: Chao leapt the wall but was caught by Qiao of the expeditionary staff. Princes, ministers, and their households were slaughtered; [24] more than ten thousand captives and two thousand horses were taken. Chao was sent to the capital and beheaded in the Jiankang market.

sentences.zh: 公之北伐也，徐道覆仍有窺窬之志，勸盧循乘虛而出，循不從。

translations.literal: During Gaozu's northern campaign Xu Daofu still harbored designs of encroachment and urged Lu Xun to strike while the moment was open; Xun would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: While Gaozu campaigned north, Xu Daofu still plotted opportunistically and urged Lu Xun to strike; Xun refused.

sentences.zh: 道覆乃至番禺說循曰：「本住嶺外，豈以理極於此，正以劉公難與為敵故也。

translations.literal: Daofu went as far as Panyu to persuade Xun, saying: "We dwell beyond the ranges—do you think we have reached our natural limit here? It is only because Duke Liu is hard to match as an enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Daofu went to Panyu and told Xun: "We live beyond the mountains—not because this is our destiny, but because Duke Liu is too dangerous to fight.

sentences.zh: 今方頓兵堅城之下，[25]未有旋日。

translations.literal: He is now halted beneath a strong city, [25] with no day of return in sight.
translations.idiomatic: He is pinned before a walled city [25] with no end in sight.

sentences.zh: 以此思歸死士，掩襲何、劉之徒，如反掌耳。

translations.literal: With that in mind, call up men ready to die for home, and strike He and Liu and their like—it would be as easy as turning the hand.
translations.idiomatic: Rally men desperate to go home and fall on He Wuji, Liu Yi, and the rest—it would be as easy as turning your hand.

sentences.zh: 不乘此機而保一日之安，若平齊之後，小息甲養眾，不過一二年間，必璽書徵君。

translations.literal: If you do not seize this chance for a single day's safety, then after Qi is pacified, when he rests the armies and nourishes his forces, within one or two years an imperial summons will surely come for you.
translations.idiomatic: Miss this opening and, once Qi is pacified and he rebuilds his armies, within a year or two an imperial edict will summon you.

sentences.zh: 若劉公自率眾至豫章，遣銳師過嶺，雖復將軍神武，恐必不能當也。

translations.literal: If Duke Liu himself leads his host to Yuzhang and sends crack troops over the ranges, even if you, General, are divinely martial, I fear you cannot withstand him.
translations.idiomatic: If Duke Liu comes to Yuzhang in person and sends elite troops over the mountains, not even your valor may save you.

sentences.zh: 今日之機，萬不可失。

translations.literal: Today's opportunity must on no account be lost.
translations.idiomatic: This chance cannot be wasted.

sentences.zh: 既剋都邑，傾其根本，劉公雖還，無能為也。

translations.literal: Once the capital is taken and their root destroyed, even if Duke Liu returns he can do nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Take the capital, destroy their base, and Duke Liu cannot recover even if he turns back.

sentences.zh: 」循從之，乃率眾過嶺。

translations.literal: " Xun followed him and led his host over the ranges.
translations.idiomatic: Xun agreed and marched his army over the mountains.

sentences.zh: 是月，寇南康、廬陵、豫章，諸郡守皆委任奔走。

translations.literal: That month they raided Nankang, Luling, and Yuzhang; the prefects of the commanderies all abandoned their posts and fled.
translations.idiomatic: That month they ravaged Nankang, Luling, and Yuzhang; every prefect fled his post.

sentences.zh: 于時平齊問未至，即馳使徵公。

translations.literal: At that time word that Qi had been pacified had not yet arrived, and an urgent messenger was sent summoning Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Before news of the fall of Qi arrived, an urgent summons reached Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 公之初剋齊也，欲停鎮下邳，清盪河、洛，既而被徵使至，即日班師。

translations.literal: When Gaozu had first conquered Qi he had intended to halt and garrison at Xiapi, clearing the Yellow and Luo rivers; but once the summons arrived he withdrew the same day.
translations.idiomatic: After taking Qi he had meant to hold Xiapi and sweep the Yellow and Luo valleys; the moment the summons came he turned back the same day.

sentences.zh: 鎮南將軍何無忌與徐道覆戰于豫章，敗績，無忌被害。

translations.literal: Defender-General He Wuji fought Xu Daofu at Yuzhang, was defeated, and Wuji was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Defender-General He Wuji fought Xu Daofu at Yuzhang, was routed, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 內外震駭。

translations.literal: Within and without the court were shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country were shaken.

sentences.zh: 朝廷欲奉乘輿北走就公，尋知賊定未至，人情小安。

translations.literal: The court wished to escort the imperial carriage north to join Gaozu; soon learning the rebels had not yet arrived, morale eased slightly.
translations.idiomatic: The court considered fleeing north to Gaozu; when it became clear the rebels had not yet reached the capital, panic subsided a little.

sentences.zh: 公至下邳，以船運輜重，自率精銳步歸。

translations.literal: Gaozu reached Xiapi, sent the baggage by ship, and himself led picked troops home on foot.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiapi he shipped the baggage and marched home at the head of an elite force.

sentences.zh: 至山陽，聞無忌被害，則慮京邑失守，乃卷甲兼行，與數十人至淮上，問行旅以朝廷消息。

translations.literal: Reaching Shanyang he heard Wuji had been killed, feared the capital would fall, rolled up his armor and pressed on day and night; with several dozen men he reached the Huai and asked travelers for news of the court.
translations.idiomatic: At Shanyang he learned of Wuji's death, feared the capital was lost, and raced on without rest. With a few dozen men he reached the Huai and questioned travelers about the court.

sentences.zh: 人曰：「賊尚未至，劉公若還，便無所憂也。

translations.literal: Someone said: "The rebels have not yet arrived; if Duke Liu returns, there will be nothing to fear.
translations.idiomatic: A traveler said: "The rebels are not here yet. If Duke Liu returns, all will be well.

sentences.zh: 」公大喜，單船過江，逕至京口，眾乃大安。

translations.literal: " Gaozu was greatly pleased, crossed the river in a single boat, went straight to Jingkou, and the people were greatly reassured.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu rejoiced, crossed the river alone in one boat, went straight to Jingkou, and the people steadied.

sentences.zh: 四月癸未，公至京師，解嚴息甲。

translations.literal: On guiwei in the fourth month Gaozu reached the capital, lifted the martial law, and rested the armies.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei in the fourth month he reached Jiankang, ended the emergency, and stood the armies down.

sentences.zh: 撫軍將軍劉毅抗表南征，公與毅書曰：「吾往習擊妖賊，曉其變態，新獲姦利，其鋒不可輕。

translations.literal: Defender-General Liu Yi submitted a memorial urging a southern campaign; Gaozu wrote to Yi: "I am accustomed to fighting these demonic rebels and know their shifts; newly victorious and emboldened, their edge must not be treated lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi memorialized for a southern campaign. Gaozu wrote: "I know these rebels and their tricks. Fresh from victory, they are dangerous.

sentences.zh: 宜須裝嚴畢，與弟同舉。

translations.literal: Wait until preparations are complete and advance together with your younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Finish your preparations and move together with your brother.

sentences.zh: 」又遣毅從弟藩往止之。

translations.literal: " He also sent Yi's cousin Fan to stop him.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Yi's cousin Fan to restrain him.

sentences.zh: 毅不從，舟師二萬，發自姑孰。

translations.literal: Yi would not listen; with twenty thousand river troops he set out from Gushu.
translations.idiomatic: Yi refused. With twenty thousand men aboard ship he sailed from Gushu.

sentences.zh: 循之初下也，使道覆向尋陽，自寇湘中諸郡。

translations.literal: When Xun first descended he sent Daofu toward Xunyang while he himself raided the commanderies of Xiangzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun first came south he sent Daofu toward Xunyang while he ravaged the Xiang river region.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史道規遣軍至長沙，為循所敗。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jing Province Daogui sent troops to Changsha and was defeated by Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhou Inspector Liu Daogui sent troops to Changsha and was beaten by Xun.

sentences.zh: 逕至巴陵，將向江陵。

translations.literal: Xun went straight to Baling, intending to advance on Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: Xun pressed on to Baling, aiming at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 道覆聞毅上，馳使報循曰：「毅兵眾甚盛，成敗事係之於此，宜并力摧之。

translations.literal: Daofu heard Yi was advancing, sent a messenger in haste to tell Xun: "Yi's troops are very numerous; success or failure hangs on this—you should combine forces and crush him.
translations.idiomatic: Daofu heard Yi was coming and urged Xun: "Yi's army is huge. Everything depends on beating him now.

sentences.zh: 若此克捷，天下無復事矣。

translations.literal: If this succeeds, there will be nothing left to do under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Win here and the empire is yours.

sentences.zh: 根本既定，不憂上面不平也。

translations.literal: Once the root is settled, there is no worry that the upper reaches will not be pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Secure the base and the upper Yangzi will follow.

sentences.zh: 」循即日發巴陵，與道覆連旗而下。

translations.literal: " That same day Xun left Baling and descended with Daofu, banners linked.
translations.idiomatic: Xun left Baling the same day and sailed downriver with Daofu, their banners joined.

sentences.zh: 別有八艚艦九枚，起四層，高十二丈。

translations.literal: Separately there were nine eight-oared warships built four stories high, twelve zhang tall.
translations.idiomatic: Nine towering four-deck warships, each twelve zhang high, sailed with them.

sentences.zh: 公以南藩覆沒，表送章綬，詔不聽。

translations.literal: Because the southern frontier had fallen, Gaozu submitted his seal and cord; the edict did not accept them.
translations.idiomatic: With the south overrun, Gaozu offered to surrender his seal and cord; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 五月，劉毅敗績于桑落洲，棄船步走，餘眾不得去者，皆為賊所擒。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Liu Yi was defeated at Sangluo Isle, abandoned his ships and fled on foot; those of his troops who could not escape were all captured by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Liu Yi was crushed at Sangluo Isle, fled on foot, and every man left behind was taken.

sentences.zh: 初循至尋陽，聞公已還，不信也。

translations.literal: When Xun first reached Xunyang he heard Gaozu had already returned and did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Xun reached Xunyang, he would not believe Gaozu had already returned.

sentences.zh: 既破毅，乃審凱入之問，並相視失色。

translations.literal: Only after defeating Yi did he confirm the news of the triumphant entry, and they looked at one another, faces drained of color.
translations.idiomatic: Only after beating Yi did he learn Gaozu was back; the rebel leaders turned pale.

sentences.zh: 循欲退還尋陽，進平江陵，據二州以抗朝廷。

translations.literal: Xun wished to withdraw to Xunyang, advance and pacify Jiangling, and hold the two provinces to resist the court.
translations.idiomatic: Xun wanted to fall back to Xunyang, take Jiangling, and hold two provinces against the court.

sentences.zh: 道覆謂宜乘勝徑進，固爭之。

translations.literal: Daofu said they should press the victory and advance directly, arguing fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Daofu insisted they strike while victorious and argued hard for a direct advance.

sentences.zh: 疑議多日，乃見從。

translations.literal: After many days of dispute he was at last obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: After days of argument Xun gave way.

sentences.zh: 毅敗問至，內外洶擾。

translations.literal: When word of Yi's defeat arrived, within and without the court was in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: News of Yi's rout threw the court into chaos.

sentences.zh: 于時北師始還，多創痍疾病。

translations.literal: At that time the northern army had just returned; many were wounded and sick.
translations.idiomatic: The northern army had just come home, battered and sick.

sentences.zh: 京師戰士，不盈數千。

translations.literal: Fighting men in the capital numbered no more than a few thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Jiankang had barely a few thousand soldiers fit to fight.

sentences.zh: 賊既破江、豫二鎮，戰士十餘萬，舟車百里不絕。

translations.literal: The rebels, having broken the Jiang and Yu garrisons, fielded more than a hundred thousand warriors; boats and wagons stretched a hundred li without break.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels now commanded more than a hundred thousand men; their fleet and train stretched a hundred li without end.

sentences.zh: 奔敗還者，並聲其雄盛。

translations.literal: Those who fled back from defeat all proclaimed their might.
translations.idiomatic: Every fugitive from the rout magnified their strength.

sentences.zh: 孟昶、諸葛長民懼寇漸逼，欲擁天子過江，公不聽，昶固請不止。

translations.literal: Meng Chang and Zhuge Changmin, fearing the bandits were closing in, wished to escort the Son of Heaven across the river; Gaozu would not listen, and Chang pressed without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Chang and Zhuge Changmin wanted to move the emperor across the river; Gaozu refused, but Chang kept pleading.

sentences.zh: 公曰：「今重鎮外傾，強寇內逼，人情危駭，莫有固志。

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "Now the great garrisons have fallen abroad and a strong enemy presses within; hearts are terrified and none hold firm resolve.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said: "Our strongholds abroad have collapsed and a powerful enemy is at the gates. Panic has eaten every fixed will.

sentences.zh: 若一旦遷動，便自瓦解土崩，江北亦豈可得至！

translations.literal: If we move the court in a single day, we will collapse of ourselves—and how could we even reach the north of the river!
translations.idiomatic: Move the court now and we dissolve at once—and we would never reach the north bank anyway.

sentences.zh: 設令得至，不過延日月耳。

translations.literal: Even if we could reach it, we would only prolong our days a little.
translations.idiomatic: Even if we crossed, we would only buy a few months.

sentences.zh: 今兵士雖少，自足以一戰。

translations.literal: Though our soldiers are few, they are enough for one battle.
translations.idiomatic: We are few, but enough for one fight.

sentences.zh: 若其克濟，則臣主同休；

translations.literal: If we succeed, ruler and minister share the blessing;
translations.idiomatic: If we win, emperor and servants survive together.

sentences.zh: 苟厄運必至，我當以死衞社稷，橫尸廟門，遂其由來以身許國之志，不能遠竄於草間求活也。

translations.literal: If doom must come, I shall die defending the altars of state, lie dead at the temple gate, and fulfill my lifelong vow to give my body to the country—I cannot flee far into the grass to save my life.
translations.idiomatic: If fate turns against us, I will die defending the altars, fall at the temple gate, and keep the vow I have always made to give my life for the state—not slink off into the wilds to live.

sentences.zh: 我計決矣，卿勿復言！

translations.literal: My decision is made—say no more!"
translations.idiomatic: My mind is made up. Speak no more!"

sentences.zh: 」昶恐其不濟，乃為表曰：「臣裕北討，眾並不同，唯臣贊裕行計，致使強賊乘間，社稷危逼，臣之罪也。

translations.literal: " Chang, fearing he would not succeed, then wrote a memorial saying: "Your servant Yu campaigned north; the multitude all disagreed, and only your servant approved Yu's plan, causing the strong rebels to seize the opening, the altars endangered and pressed—this is your servant's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing defeat, Chang wrote a memorial: "I alone urged Yu's northern campaign against the court's judgment, letting the rebels strike while we were exposed. The altars are in peril because of me.

sentences.zh: 今謹引分以謝天下。

translations.literal: Now I respectfully accept punishment to apologize to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I accept punishment to atone before the realm.

sentences.zh: 」封表畢，乃仰藥而死。

translations.literal: " Having sealed the memorial he took poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: He sealed the memorial and drank poison.

sentences.zh: 於是大開賞募，投身赴義者，一同登京城之科。

translations.literal: Thereupon great rewards and enlistments were opened; those who came forward in righteous service were all enrolled on the capital rolls alike.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu opened the treasury and the rolls: every volunteer was enrolled on the capital service list.

sentences.zh: 發居民治石頭城，建牙戒嚴。

translations.literal: The populace was mobilized to repair Shitou fortress; banners were raised and martial law proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Civilians were called to repair Shitou fortress; the camp was set and the alarm sounded.

sentences.zh: 時議者謂宜分兵守諸津要。

translations.literal: At the time debaters said troops should be divided to hold the key crossings.
translations.idiomatic: Some argued for splitting the army to hold every crossing.

sentences.zh: 公以為：「賊眾我寡，若分兵屯，則人測虛實。

translations.literal: Gaozu held: "The rebels are many and we are few; if we divide and garrison, men will gauge our strength.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu disagreed: "They outnumber us. Split the army and they learn our weakness.

sentences.zh: 且一處失利，則沮三軍之心。

translations.literal: Moreover, if one place is lost, the heart of the three armies is broken.
translations.idiomatic: Lose one post and the whole army loses heart.

sentences.zh: 今聚眾石頭，隨宜應赴，既令賊無以測多少，又於眾力不分。

translations.literal: Now gather the host at Shitou and respond as needed—this both keeps the enemy from measuring our numbers and does not split our strength.
translations.idiomatic: Mass at Shitou and respond where needed. They cannot count us, and our strength stays whole.

sentences.zh: 若徒旅轉集，徐更論之耳。

translations.literal: If more troops keep arriving, we can discuss it again later.
translations.idiomatic: If reinforcements gather, we can reconsider.

sentences.zh: 」移屯石頭，乃柵淮斷查浦。

translations.literal: " He moved camp to Shitou, palisaded the Huai, and blocked Zha Pu.
translations.idiomatic: He shifted to Shitou, fortified the Huai line, and blocked Zha Pu.

sentences.zh: 既而羣賊大至，公策之曰：「賊若於新亭直進，其鋒不可當，宜且回避，勝負之事，未可量也。

translations.literal: Soon the rebel masses arrived in force; Gaozu calculated: "If the rebels advance straight from Xinting, their edge cannot be met—we should for the moment avoid them, and victory or defeat cannot yet be measured.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel host arrived, Gaozu judged: "If they drive straight from Xinting, their momentum is unstoppable. We must dodge them first.

sentences.zh: 若回泊西岸，此成擒耳。」

translations.literal: If they turn and moor on the western bank, they are as good as captured."
translations.idiomatic: If they anchor on the western bank, we have them."

sentences.zh: 道覆欲自新亭、白石焚舟而上。

translations.literal: Daofu wished to burn the boats at Xinting and Baishi and advance upstream.
translations.idiomatic: Daofu wanted to burn their boats at Xinting and Baishi and fight upstream.

sentences.zh: 循多疑少決，每欲以萬全為慮，謂道覆曰：「大軍未至，孟昶便望風自裁，大勢言之，自當計日潰亂。

translations.literal: Xun was suspicious and slow to decide, always seeking perfect safety; he told Daofu: "The great army has not yet arrived, yet Meng Chang killed himself at the first rumor—in the larger trend, collapse should come day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was cautious to a fault. He told Daofu: "The main army is not here, yet Meng Chang already killed himself at a rumor. By every sign the court should fall apart daily.

sentences.zh: 今決勝負於一朝，既非必定之道，且殺傷士卒，不如按兵待之。

translations.literal: To settle victory or defeat in a single morning is not a certain course, and besides it kills soldiers—it is better to hold the army and wait.
translations.idiomatic: Why gamble everything in one morning, bleed our men, when we can wait?

sentences.zh: 」公于時登石頭城以望循軍，初見引向新亭，公顧左右失色。

translations.literal: " At that time Gaozu climbed Shitou fortress to watch Xun's army; when he first saw them heading for Xinting, he looked to those beside him, faces changed.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu watched from Shitou. When he saw the rebels heading for Xinting, his officers turned pale.

sentences.zh: 既而回泊蔡洲。

translations.literal: Then they turned and moored at Cai Isle.
translations.idiomatic: Then the rebels swung aside and anchored at Cai Isle.

sentences.zh: 道覆猶欲上，循禁之。

translations.literal: Daofu still wished to advance; Xun forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: Daofu still wanted to attack; Xun stopped him.

sentences.zh: 自是眾軍轉集，修治越城，築查浦、藥園、廷尉三壘，皆守以實眾。

translations.literal: From then on the armies kept gathering; Yue city was repaired, and three forts were built at Zha Pu, Yaoyuan, and the Court of Justice, all held with solid forces.
translations.idiomatic: Reinforcements kept arriving. Yue city was repaired and three forts—Zha Pu, Yaoyuan, and the Court of Justice—were garrisoned in strength.

sentences.zh: 冠軍將軍劉敬宣屯北郊，輔國將軍孟懷玉屯丹陽郡西，建武將軍王仲德屯越城，廣武將軍劉懷默屯建陽門外。

translations.literal: Champion-General Liu Jingxuan garrisoned the northern suburbs; Assistant-General Meng Huaiyu garrisoned west of Danyang Commandery; General Who Establishes Might Wang Zhongde garrisoned Yue city; General of Expansive Might Liu Huaimo garrisoned outside the Jianyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jingxuan held the north suburbs; Meng Huaiyu the west of Danyang; Wang Zhongde Yue city; Liu Huaimo outside the Jianyang Gate.

sentences.zh: [26]使寧朔將軍索邈領鮮卑具裝虎班突騎千餘匹，皆被練五色，自淮北至于新亭。

translations.literal: [26] He sent General of Ning-shuo Suo Miao to lead more than a thousand fully armored Xianbei tiger-striped shock cavalry, all draped in five-colored white silk, from north of the Huai to Xinting.
translations.idiomatic: [26] He sent Suo Miao with more than a thousand armored Xianbei cataphracts draped in five-colored silk from north of the Huai to Xinting.

sentences.zh: 賊並聚觀，咸畏憚之；

translations.literal: The rebels all gathered to watch and were awed and afraid;
translations.idiomatic: The rebels watched from afar, awed and afraid.

sentences.zh: 然猶冀京邑及三吳有應之者。

translations.literal: yet they still hoped that the capital and the Three Wu would have men who would respond.
translations.idiomatic: Yet they still hoped the capital and the Three Wu would rise for them.

sentences.zh: 遣十餘艦來拔石頭柵，公命神弩射之，發輒摧陷，循乃止不復攻柵。

translations.literal: They sent more than ten ships to pull up the Shitou palisade; Gaozu ordered divine crossbows to shoot them—each shot smashed and sank them—and Xun then stopped and did not attack the palisade again.
translations.idiomatic: They sent a dozen ships to tear out the Shitou palisade. Gaozu's heavy crossbows smashed every one; Xun gave up the attempt.

sentences.zh: 設伏兵於南岸，使羸老悉乘舟艦向白石。

translations.literal: He set ambush troops on the south bank and had the weak and old all board ships toward Baishi.
translations.idiomatic: He hid troops on the south bank and sent the old and weak aboard ships toward Baishi as bait.

sentences.zh: 公憂其從白石步上，乃率劉毅、諸葛長民北出拒之，留參軍徐赤特戍南岸，命堅守勿動。

translations.literal: Gaozu feared they would land at Baishi on foot; he therefore led Liu Yi and Zhuge Changmin north to meet them, leaving Staff Officer Xu Chite to garrison the south bank with orders to hold firm and not move.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing a landing at Baishi, Gaozu led Liu Yi and Zhuge Changmin north while Xu Chite held the south bank under strict orders not to stir.

sentences.zh: 公既去，賊焚查浦步上，赤特軍戰敗，死沒有百餘人。

translations.literal: Once Gaozu had gone, the rebels burned Zha Pu and came ashore; Chite's army was defeated and more than a hundred were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Once Gaozu left, the rebels burned Zha Pu and came ashore. Chite was beaten; more than a hundred died.

sentences.zh: 赤特棄餘眾，單舸濟淮。

translations.literal: Chite abandoned the remainder of his force and crossed the Huai in a single boat.
translations.idiomatic: Chite abandoned his men and fled alone across the Huai in one boat.

sentences.zh: 賊遂率數萬屯丹陽郡。

translations.literal: The rebels then led several tens of thousands to encamp in Danyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels marched several tens of thousands into Danyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 公率諸軍馳歸。

translations.literal: Gaozu led the armies back at speed.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu raced the army home.

sentences.zh: 眾憂賊過，咸謂公當徑還拒戰。

translations.literal: The men feared the rebels had already passed; all said Gaozu should turn back at once to fight.
translations.idiomatic: His officers feared the enemy had already broken through and urged an immediate counterattack.

sentences.zh: 公先分軍還石頭，眾莫之曉。

translations.literal: Gaozu first sent part of the army back to Shitou; none understood why.
translations.idiomatic: First he sent part of the force back to Shitou, to everyone's bafflement.

sentences.zh: 解甲息士，洗浴飲食之，乃出列陳於南塘。

translations.literal: He ordered the men to doff armor and rest, bathe, eat, and drink; then he formed ranks and drew up at Nantang.
translations.idiomatic: He had the men stand down, wash, eat, and drink—then formed them in battle order at Nantang.

sentences.zh: 以赤特違處分，斬之。

translations.literal: Because Chite had disobeyed orders, he was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He executed Chite for disobeying orders.

sentences.zh: 命參軍褚叔度、朱齡石率勁勇千餘人過淮。

translations.literal: He ordered Staff Officers Chu Shudu and Zhu Lingshi to lead more than a thousand picked men across the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Chu Shudu and Zhu Lingshi with more than a thousand picked men across the Huai.

sentences.zh: [27]羣賊數千，皆長刀矛鋋，精甲曜日，奮躍爭進。

translations.literal: [27] Several thousand rebels, all with long sabers, spears, and ge halberds, in bright armor flashing in the sun, leaped forward vying to advance.
translations.idiomatic: [27] Several thousand rebels came on with long blades, spears, and ge halberds, armor blazing in the sun, fighting to be first.

sentences.zh: 齡石所領多鮮卑，善步矟，並結陳以待之。

translations.literal: Most of those Lingshi led were Xianbei, skilled with infantry spears; they all formed ranks and waited.
translations.idiomatic: Lingshi's men were mostly Xianbei spearmen; they locked shields and waited.

sentences.zh: 賊短兵弗能抗，死傷者數百人，乃退走。

translations.literal: At close quarters the rebels could not resist; several hundred were killed or wounded, and they then retreated.
translations.idiomatic: At close quarters the rebels could not break them; several hundred fell, and the rest withdrew.

sentences.zh: 會日莫，眾亦歸。

translations.literal: As night fell the troops also returned.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk both sides withdrew.

sentences.zh: 劉毅之敗，豫州主簿袁興國反叛，據歷陽以應賊。

translations.literal: After Liu Yi's defeat, Registrar of Yu Province Yuan Xingguo rebelled, seized Liyang, and joined the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: After Yi's rout, Yu Province registrar Yuan Xingguo rebelled, seized Liyang, and sided with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 琅邪內史魏順之遣將謝寶討斬之。

translations.literal: Interior Minister of Langya Wei Shunzhi sent his general Xie Bao to attack and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Langya interior minister Wei Shunzhi sent Xie Bao to attack and kill him.

sentences.zh: 興國司馬襲寶，順之不救而退，公怒斬之。

translations.literal: Xingguo's Major struck at Bao; Shunzhi did not rescue him and withdrew—Gaozu in anger beheaded Shunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Xingguo's major ambushed Bao; Shunzhi refused to help and retreated. Gaozu had Shunzhi executed.

sentences.zh: 順之，詠之之弟也。

translations.literal: Shunzhi was the younger brother of Yongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Shunzhi was Yongzhi's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 於是功臣震懾，莫敢不用命。

translations.literal: Thereupon the meritorious ministers were awed and none dared disobey orders.
translations.idiomatic: From then on every commander obeyed without question.

sentences.zh: 六月，更授公太尉、中書監，加黃鉞。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Gaozu was again appointed Grand Commandant and Supervisor of the Secretariat, with the yellow battle-axe added.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he was again offered Grand Commandant, Supervisor of the Secretariat, and the yellow axe.

sentences.zh: 受黃鉞，餘固辭。

translations.literal: He accepted the yellow axe; the rest he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He took the axe and refused the rest.

sentences.zh: 以司馬庾悅為建威將軍、江州刺史，自東陽出豫章。

translations.literal: Staff Officer Yu Yue was made General Who Establishes Might and Inspector of Jiang Province, to march from Dongyang toward Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yue was made General Who Establishes Might and Inspector of Jiang Province and sent from Dongyang toward Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 七月庚申，羣賊自蔡洲南走，還屯尋陽。

translations.literal: On gengshen in the seventh month the rebel masses fled south from Cai Isle and returned to encamp at Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen in the seventh month the rebels fled south from Cai Isle back to Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 遣輔國將軍王仲德、廣川太守劉鍾、河間太守蒯恩追之。

translations.literal: Assistant-General Wang Zhongde, Administrator of Guangchuan Liu Zhong, and Administrator of Hejian Kuai En were sent in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongde, Liu Zhong, and Kuai En were sent after them.

sentences.zh: 公還東府，大治水軍，皆大艦重樓，高者十餘丈。

translations.literal: Gaozu returned to the Eastern Headquarters and greatly expanded the river army—all large ships with layered towers, the tallest more than ten zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Back at the Eastern Headquarters he rebuilt the fleet with towering decked warships more than ten zhang high.

sentences.zh: 盧循遣其大將荀林寇江陵，[28]桓謙先於江陵奔羌，又自羌入蜀，偽主譙縱以為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: Lu Xun sent his great general Xun Lin to raid Jiangling; [28] Huan Qian had earlier fled from Jiangling to the Qiang, then from the Qiang entered Shu; the false ruler Qiao Zong made him Inspector of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun sent General Xun Lin against Jiangling; [28] Huan Qian had fled Jiangling to the Qiang, then entered Shu, where Qiao Zong made him Jingzhou inspector.

sentences.zh: 謙及譙道福率軍二萬，出寇江陵，適與林會，相去百餘里。

translations.literal: Qian and Qiao Daofu led twenty thousand troops to raid Jiangling; they happened to meet Lin, less than a hundred li apart.
translations.idiomatic: Qian and Qiao Daofu marched twenty thousand men against Jiangling and met Lin a hundred li away.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史道規斬謙于枝江，破林於江津，追至竹町斬之。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jing Province Daogui beheaded Qian at Zhijiang, broke Lin at Jiangjin, pursued to Zhuting, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Daogui killed Qian at Zhijiang, routed Lin at Jiangjin, and hunted him down at Zhuting.

sentences.zh: 初循之走也，公知其必寇江陵，登遣淮陵內史索邈領馬軍步道援荊州。

translations.literal: When Xun first fled, Gaozu knew he would surely raid Jiangling and at once sent Huailing Interior Minister Suo Miao to lead mounted troops by land to aid Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun fled, Gaozu knew Jiangling would be threatened and sent Suo Miao with cavalry overland to reinforce Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 又遣建威將軍孫季高率眾三千，自海道襲番禺。

translations.literal: He also sent General Who Establishes Might Sun Jigao with three thousand men by sea to strike Panyu.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Sun Jigao with three thousand men by sea against Panyu.

sentences.zh: 江州刺史庾悅至五畝嶠，賊遣千餘人據斷嶠道，悅前驅鄱陽太守虞丘進攻破之。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jiang Province Yu Yue reached Wumu Pass; the rebels sent more than a thousand men to hold and block the pass road; Yue's vanguard, Administrator of Poyang Yu Qiu, broke through them.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yue reached Wumu Pass, where rebels blocked the road; his vanguard Yu Qiu broke through.

sentences.zh: 公治兵大辦。

translations.literal: Gaozu's military preparations were complete.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu's preparations were complete.

sentences.zh: 十月，率兗州刺史劉藩、寧朔將軍檀韶等舟師南伐。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he led the river army south with Inspector of Yan Province Liu Fan, General of Ning-shuo Tan Shao, and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he sailed south with Liu Fan, Tan Shao, and the fleet.

sentences.zh: 以後將軍劉毅監太尉留守府，後事皆委焉。

translations.literal: Rear-General Liu Yi was made supervisor of the Grand Commandant's rear headquarters; all later affairs were entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi was left to supervise the capital in Gaozu's absence.

sentences.zh: 是月，徐道覆率眾三萬寇江陵。

translations.literal: That month Xu Daofu led thirty thousand men to raid Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: That month Xu Daofu struck Jiangling with thirty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史道規又大破之，斬首萬餘級，道覆走還盆口。

translations.literal: Inspector of Jing Province Daogui again routed them greatly, beheaded more than ten thousand, and Daofu fled back to Penkou.
translations.idiomatic: Daogui crushed him again, took more than ten thousand heads, and Daofu fled to Penkou.

sentences.zh: 初公之遣索邈也，邈在道為賊所斷，道覆敗後方達。

translations.literal: When Gaozu had first sent Suo Miao, Miao was cut off on the road by rebels and only arrived after Daofu's defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Miao had been cut off en route and arrived only after Daofu's defeat.

sentences.zh: 自循東下，江陵斷絕京邑之問，傳者皆云已沒。

translations.literal: From the time Xun descended eastward, contact between Jiangling and the capital was severed; messengers all said the city had fallen.
translations.idiomatic: While Xun marched east, word from Jiangling ceased; rumor said it was lost.

sentences.zh: 及邈至，方知循走。

translations.literal: When Miao arrived they finally learned Xun had fled.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Miao arrived did they learn Xun had already fled.

sentences.zh: 循初自蔡洲南走，留其親黨范崇民五千人，高艦百餘，戍南陵。

translations.literal: When Xun first fled south from Cai Isle he left his close partisan Fan Chongmin with five thousand men and more than a hundred tall ships to garrison Nanling.
translations.idiomatic: Fleeing south from Cai Isle, Xun left Fan Chongmin with five thousand men and a hundred warships at Nanling.

sentences.zh: 王仲德等聞大軍且至，乃進攻之。

translations.literal: Wang Zhongde and the others, hearing the great army was about to arrive, advanced to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the main army was coming, Wang Zhongde attacked.

sentences.zh: 十一月，大破崇民軍，焚其舟艦，收其散卒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month they routed Chongmin's army, burned their ships, and gathered the scattered troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month they smashed Chongmin, burned his fleet, and gathered the survivors.

sentences.zh: 循廣州守兵，不以海道為防。

translations.literal: The garrison troops Xun had left at Guangzhou did not guard the sea route.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's garrison at Guangzhou never guarded the sea lanes.

sentences.zh: 是月，建威將軍孫季高乘海奄至，而城池峻整，兵猶數千。

translations.literal: That month General Who Establishes Might Sun Jigao came suddenly by sea; though the walls were high and strong, there were still several thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: That month Sun Jigao appeared suddenly from the sea. The walls were strong, but several thousand defenders remained.

sentences.zh: 季高焚賊舟艦，悉力而上，四面攻之，即日屠其城。

translations.literal: Jigao burned the rebel ships, brought all his strength to bear, attacked from four sides, and sacked the city the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Jigao burned their ships, assaulted from every side, and took the city the same day.

sentences.zh: 循父以輕舟奔始興。

translations.literal: Xun's father fled in a light boat to Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's father fled by light boat to Shixing.

sentences.zh: 季高撫其舊民，戮其親黨，勒兵謹守。

translations.literal: Jigao comforted the old populace, executed the partisans, and kept the troops under strict guard.
translations.idiomatic: Jigao pacified the people, killed the partisans, and held the city in strength.

sentences.zh: 初公之遣季高也，眾咸以海道艱遠，必至為難；

translations.literal: When Gaozu first sent Jigao, the multitude all thought the sea route arduous and distant and that disaster was sure to come;
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu sent Jigao, everyone said the sea route was too long and risky.

sentences.zh: 且分撤見力，二三非要。

translations.literal: moreover, to divide and withdraw present strength was two or three parts mistaken.
translations.idiomatic: Splitting his forces seemed folly on every count.

sentences.zh: 公不從。

translations.literal: Gaozu would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 敕季高曰：「大軍十二月之交，必破妖虜。

translations.literal: He instructed Jigao: "When the great army crosses the twelfth month, it will surely break the demonic rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He told Jigao: "By mid-twelfth month the main army will break the rebels.

sentences.zh: 卿今時當至廣州，傾其巢窟，令賊奔走之日，無所歸投。

translations.literal: You must now reach Guangzhou, overturn their nest, and leave them nowhere to flee when they run.
translations.idiomatic: Reach Guangzhou now, destroy their nest, and cut off their retreat.

sentences.zh: 」季高受命而行，如期剋捷。

translations.literal: " Jigao received the order and marched; on schedule he achieved victory.
translations.idiomatic: Jigao sailed on time and won on schedule.

sentences.zh: 循方治兵旅舟艦，設諸攻備。

translations.literal: Xun was just then organizing troops and ships and setting up every sort of attack preparation.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was still fitting out ships and siege gear.

sentences.zh: 公欲御以長算，乃屯軍雷池。

translations.literal: Gaozu wished to meet him with long strategy and therefore encamped the army at Leichi.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu chose patience and encamped at Leichi.

sentences.zh: 賊揚聲不攻雷池，當乘流逕下。

translations.literal: The rebels proclaimed they would not attack Leichi but would ride the current straight downstream.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels announced they would bypass Leichi and sail straight downriver.

sentences.zh: 公知其欲戰，且慮賊戰敗，或於京江入海，遣王仲德以水艦二百於吉陽下斷之。

translations.literal: Gaozu knew they wanted battle and, fearing that if defeated they might enter the sea at Jingjiang, sent Wang Zhongde with two hundred warships to block them below Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu knew they meant to fight and, fearing a sea escape, sent Wang Zhongde with two hundred ships to block the Jingjiang estuary.

sentences.zh: 十二月，循、道覆率眾數萬，方艦而下，前後相抗，莫見舳艫之際。
