translations.literal: In the twelfth month Xun and Daofu led several tens of thousands in square ships descending; front and rear pressed against one another, and one could not see where the sterns and prows ended.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Xun and Daofu came downriver with tens of thousands in decked warships, stern to prow without end.

sentences.zh: 公悉出輕利鬭艦，躬提幡鼓，命眾軍齊力擊之。

translations.literal: Gaozu sent out all his light fighting ships, personally took the banner drum, and ordered the armies to strike together with combined strength.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu sent out every light warship, took the drum himself, and ordered a mass attack.

sentences.zh: 又上步騎於西岸。

translations.literal: He also sent infantry and cavalry up on the western bank.
translations.idiomatic: Infantry and cavalry lined the western bank.

sentences.zh: 右軍參軍庾樂生乘艦不進，斬而徇之。

translations.literal: Right Army Staff Officer Yu Lesheng aboard ship would not advance; he was beheaded and the deed displayed.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Lesheng hung back in his ship; Gaozu had him beheaded as an example.

sentences.zh: 於是眾軍並踊騰爭先。

translations.literal: Thereupon all the armies leaped and vied to be first.
translations.idiomatic: Then every unit surged forward at once.

sentences.zh: 軍中多萬鈞神弩，所至莫不摧陷。

translations.literal: The army had many ten-thousand-jin divine crossbows; wherever they reached nothing failed to be smashed and sunk.
translations.idiomatic: The army fielded mighty ten-thousand-jin crossbows that smashed everything in range.

sentences.zh: 公中流蹙之，因風水之勢，賊艦悉泊西岸。

translations.literal: Gaozu drove them into midstream and, using the force of wind and water, all the rebel ships were forced to moor on the western bank.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu drove them midstream; wind and current washed every rebel ship onto the western bank.

sentences.zh: 岸上軍先備火具，[29]乃投火焚之，煙爓張天，賊眾大敗，追奔至夜乃歸。

translations.literal: The troops on the bank had prepared fire equipment beforehand, [29] then cast fire and burned them; smoke and flames filled the sky; the rebel masses were greatly defeated, and the pursuit ran until night before they returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shore troops had fire ready [29] and set the fleet ablaze. Smoke filled the sky; the rebels broke; the pursuit lasted until night.

sentences.zh: 循等還尋陽。

translations.literal: Xun and the others returned to Xunyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xun fled back to Xunyang.

sentences.zh: 初分遣步軍，莫不疑怪，及燒賊艦，眾乃悅服。

translations.literal: At first, when he had divided and sent the infantry, none failed to be puzzled; only after the rebel ships were burned did the masses approve and submit.
translations.idiomatic: At first his dispatch of infantry baffled everyone; after the burning of the fleet they understood.

sentences.zh: 召王仲德，請還為前驅。

translations.literal: He summoned Wang Zhongde and asked him to return as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He recalled Wang Zhongde as vanguard.

sentences.zh: 留輔國將軍孟懷玉守雷池。

translations.literal: Assistant-General Meng Huaiyu was left to hold Leichi.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Huaiyu was left to hold Leichi.

sentences.zh: 循聞大軍上，欲走向豫章，乃悉力柵斷左里。

translations.literal: Xun, hearing the great army was advancing upstream, wished to flee toward Yuzhang and therefore used all his strength to palisade and block Zuoli.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the main army was coming upstream, Xun tried to flee to Yuzhang and fortified Zuoli.

sentences.zh: 大軍至左里，將戰，公所執麾竿折，折幡沈水，眾並怪懼。

translations.literal: When the great army reached Zuoli and was about to give battle, the command staff Gaozu held snapped, the banner sank in the water, and the masses were all alarmed and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: At Zuoli, as battle began, Gaozu's command staff snapped and the banner sank—his men were terrified.

sentences.zh: 公歡笑曰：「往年覆舟之戰，幡竿亦折，今者復然，賊必破矣。

translations.literal: Gaozu laughed and said: "In the battle of overturned boats in former years the banner staff also snapped; now it happens again—the rebels will surely be broken.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu laughed: "The year our boats capsized, the staff snapped too. It snaps again—the rebels will break.

sentences.zh: 」即攻柵而進。

translations.literal: " He at once attacked the palisade and advanced.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked the palisade at once.

sentences.zh: 遁兵雖殊死戰，弗能禁。

translations.literal: The fleeing soldiers fought desperately but could not be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The defenders fought to the death but could not hold.

sentences.zh: 諸軍乘勝奔之，循單舸走。

translations.literal: The armies pressed the victory in pursuit; Xun fled in a single boat.
translations.idiomatic: The armies surged after them; Xun escaped in one boat.

sentences.zh: 所殺及投水死，凡萬餘人。

translations.literal: Those killed and those who drowned numbered more than ten thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten thousand were killed or drowned.

sentences.zh: 納其降附，宥其逼略。

translations.literal: Those who surrendered were accepted; those forced into service were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Surrenderers were taken in; the coerced were forgiven.

sentences.zh: 遣劉藩、孟懷玉輕軍追之。

translations.literal: Liu Fan and Meng Huaiyu with light troops were sent in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fan and Meng Huaiyu pursued with light troops.

sentences.zh: 循收散卒，尚有數千人，逕還廣州。

translations.literal: Xun gathered scattered troops; he still had several thousand men and went straight back to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xun rallied a few thousand survivors and fled to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 道覆還保始興。

translations.literal: Daofu returned to hold Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Daofu fell back to Shixing.

sentences.zh: 公旋自左里。

translations.literal: Gaozu turned back from Zuoli.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu withdrew from Zuoli.

sentences.zh: 天子遣侍中、黃門勞師于行所。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven sent Palace Attendant and Yellow Gate to comfort the army at the place of march.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a palace attendant and yellow-gate officer to congratulate the army on campaign.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes.
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes.

sentences.zh: 彭城縣綏輿里人 各本並奪去「輿」字。

translations.literal: A man of Suiyu Lane, Pengcheng County—every edition omits the character "yu."
translations.idiomatic: Regarding "a man of Suiyu Lane, Pengcheng County": every edition drops the character yu.

sentences.zh: 御覽一二八引徐爰宋書作「彭城綏輿里人」。

translations.literal: Imperial Readings 128, citing Xu Ai's Book of Song, reads "a man of Peng Suoyu Lane."
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Readings 128, citing Xu Ai's Book of Song, has "Peng Suoyu Lane."

sentences.zh: 符瑞志中附會祥瑞，云：元嘉二十一年，「甘露降彭城綏輿里」。

translations.literal: Records of Omens, attaching auspicious signs, says: in the twenty-first year of Yuanjia, "sweet dew fell on Suoyu Lane, Pengcheng."
translations.idiomatic: Records of Omens reads: in Yuanjia 21, "sweet dew fell on Suoyu Lane, Pengcheng."

sentences.zh: 南史亦有「輿」字。

translations.literal: The History of the Southern Dynasties also has the character "yu."
translations.idiomatic: The History of the Southern Dynasties also preserves yu.

sentences.zh: 今據補。

translations.literal: Now restored on that evidence.
translations.idiomatic: The character is restored here accordingly.

sentences.zh: 恩以彭排自載 「彭排」各本並作「鼓排」。

translations.literal: En carried himself on a pengpai shield—"pengpai" appears as "gupai" in every edition.
translations.idiomatic: Sun En "carried himself on a pengpai shield"; every edition reads gupai instead of pengpai.

sentences.zh: 御覽三五七引晉安帝紀作「彭排」，今據改。

translations.literal: Imperial Readings 357, citing the Annals of Emperor An of Jin, reads "pengpai"; changed accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Readings 357, citing the Jin Annals of Emperor An, has pengpai; the text is changed accordingly.

sentences.zh: 王鎮惡傳亦有「見軍人擔彭排戰具」語，釋名：「彭排，彭，旁也。

translations.literal: The biography of Wang Zhen'e also has the phrase "seeing soldiers carrying pengpai battle gear"; Etymological Names says: "Pengpai—peng means beside.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen'e's biography also mentions "soldiers carrying pengpai battle gear." Etymological Names explains: "Pengpai: peng means beside.

sentences.zh: 在旁排敵禦攻也。」

translations.literal: It wards off attack from the side."
translations.idiomatic: It shields against flank attack."

sentences.zh: 領水軍追討至鬱洲 「討」各本作「罰」，據元龜一八四改。

translations.literal: Leading the river army in pursuit and attack as far as Yuzhou—"attack" appears as "punish" in every edition; changed per Essentials of the Yuan Dynasty 184.
translations.idiomatic: In "leading the river army in pursuit and attack as far as Yuzhou," every edition reads "punish" instead of "attack"; changed per Yuan Dynasty Essentials 184.

sentences.zh: 通鑑亦作「討孫恩於鬱洲」。

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror also reads "attacking Sun En at Yuzhou."
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror also reads "attacking Sun En at Yuzhou."

sentences.zh: 高祖與牢之甥東海何無忌並固諫不從 「諫」各本並作「請」，據南史改。

translations.literal: Gaozu and Laozhi's nephew He Wuji of Donghai both firmly remonstrated and would not follow—"remonstrate" appears as "request" in every edition; changed per History of the Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu and Laozhi's nephew He Wuji of Donghai "firmly remonstrated and would not follow"; every edition reads "request" instead of "remonstrate"; changed per the Southern History.

sentences.zh: 憑之從子韶韶弟祗隆道濟 各本不疊「韶」字，又「道濟」上有「與叔」二字。

translations.literal: Pingzhi's nephew Shao, Shao's younger brothers Zhi, Long, and Daoji—every edition fails to repeat "Shao," and before "Daoji" stand the two characters "with uncle."
translations.idiomatic: Pingzhi's nephew Shao, Shao's younger brothers Zhi, Long, and Daoji: editions omit the repeated Shao and insert "with uncle" before Daoji.

sentences.zh: 孫虨宋書考論云：「祗、隆、道濟並韶弟，依文義當疊『韶』字。

translations.literal: Sun Ban's Collation of the Book of Song says: "Zhi, Long, and Daoji were all Shao's younger brothers; by the sense of the text the character Shao should be repeated.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ban's Collation argues: "Zhi, Long, and Daoji were Shao's brothers; Shao should be repeated.

sentences.zh: 」今據孫說補。

translations.literal: " Now supplemented on Sun's authority.
translations.idiomatic: The repetition is added on Sun's authority.

sentences.zh: 張熷讀史舉正云：「韶、祗、道濟並兄弟，此云『與叔』，誤。

translations.literal: Zhang Huang's Corrections in Reading History says: "Shao, Zhi, and Daoji were all brothers; to say 'with uncle' here is an error.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Huang's Corrections in Reading History says: "Shao, Zhi, and Daoji were brothers; 'with uncle' is wrong.

sentences.zh: 」今據張說刪。

translations.literal: " Now deleted on Zhang's authority.
translations.idiomatic: Those two characters are deleted on Zhang's authority.

sentences.zh: 東莞臧熹 「熹」各本並作「喜」，據臧質傳改。

translations.literal: Zang Xi of Dongguan—"Xi" appears as "Xi (joy)" in every edition; changed per the biography of Zang Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Xi of Dongguan: every edition reads the homophone for "joy" instead of Xi; changed per Zang Zhi's biography.

sentences.zh: 既而嫌邁不執安穆使得逃去 「嫌」各本並作「廉」，據通鑑晉安帝元興三年改。

translations.literal: Then, resenting that Mai did not seize An Mu and let him escape—"resent" appears as "incorruptible" in every edition; changed per Comprehensive Mirror, third year of Yuanxing under Emperor An of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Then "resenting that Mai did not seize An Mu and let him escape": every edition reads "incorruptible" instead of "resent"; changed per Comprehensive Mirror, Yuanxing 3.

sentences.zh: 玄又遣武騎將軍庾禕之 晉書桓玄傳作「武衞將軍庾頤之」。

translations.literal: Xuan also sent Martial Cavalry General Yu Yi—Jin History, biography of Huan Xuan, reads "Defender General Yu Yi."
translations.idiomatic: Xuan also sent Martial Cavalry General Yu Yi: Jin History, Huan Xuan's biography, reads Defender General Yu Yi.

sentences.zh: 立留臺官 三朝本、毛本作「立留臺官」。

translations.literal: Establish rear-capital officials—Three-Dynasty edition and Mao edition read "establish rear-capital officials."
translations.idiomatic: Establish rear-capital officials: the Three-Dynasty and Mao editions read "establish rear-capital officials."

sentences.zh: 北監本、殿本、局本作「立留臺總百官」。

translations.literal: Northern Directorate edition, Palace edition, and Bureau edition read "establish rear-capital to oversee the hundred officials."
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Directorate, Palace, and Bureau editions read "establish rear-capital to oversee the hundred officials."

sentences.zh: 通鑑作「立留臺百官」。

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror reads "establish rear-capital hundred officials."
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror reads "establish rear-capital hundred officials."

sentences.zh: 按時晉安帝尚在尋陽，故建康稱留臺。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor An of Jin was still at Xunyang, hence Jiankang was called the rear capital.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor An was still at Xunyang, so Jiankang was termed the rear capital.

sentences.zh: 據下文眾欲推劉裕領揚州，裕固辭，則此時劉裕必無總百官之事。

translations.literal: According to the text below, when the multitude wished to push Liu Yu to head Yang Province and Yu firmly declined, at this time Liu Yu could not have had the affair of overseeing the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: Below, the court tries to make Liu Yu head Yang Province and he refuses—so he cannot yet have overseen all officials.

sentences.zh: 以此知作「總百官」者，誤。

translations.literal: From this one knows that reading "oversee the hundred officials" is an error.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore "oversee the hundred officials" is wrong.

sentences.zh: 尚書王嘏率百官奉迎乘輿 「王嘏」各本並作「王假」，據南史及通鑑改。

translations.literal: Secretary Wang Gu led the hundred officials to welcome the imperial carriage—"Wang Gu" appears as "Wang Jia" in every edition; changed per History of the Southern Dynasties and Comprehensive Mirror.
translations.idiomatic: Secretary Wang Gu led the officials to welcome the emperor: every edition reads Wang Jia; changed per Southern History and Comprehensive Mirror.

sentences.zh: 晉書王導傳：「嗣孫嘏，歷領軍、尚書。」

translations.literal: Jin History, biography of Wang Dao: "His descendant Gu held the posts of Defender-General and Secretary."
translations.idiomatic: Jin History, Wang Dao's biography: "His descendant Gu served as Defender-General and Secretary."

sentences.zh: 領軍將軍徐州刺史 御覽一二八引徐爰宋書、魏書島夷劉裕傳、建康實錄並作「鎮軍將軍」。

translations.literal: Defender-General and Inspector of Xu Province—Imperial Readings 128 citing Xu Ai's Book of Song, Wei History biography of the barbarian Liu Yu, and Records of Jiankang all read "General Who Guards the Army."
translations.idiomatic: Defender-General and Inspector of Xu Province: Imperial Readings 128, Wei History's Liu Yu biography, and Records of Jiankang all read General Who Guards the Army.

sentences.zh: 孫虨宋書考論云：「領軍與都督刺史異職，晉書及宋本紀同卷後進位侍中詔皆作『鎮軍將軍』，則都督刺史加號也。

translations.literal: Sun Ban's Collation of the Book of Song says: "Defender-General and governor-inspector are different offices; Jin History and the annals of Song in this same fascicle, in the later edict advancing him to Palace Attendant, both read General Who Guards the Army—thus it is the added title of governor-inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ban notes: Defender-General differs from governor-inspector; Jin History and later Song annals use General Who Guards the Army as the combined title.

sentences.zh: 當從之。

translations.literal: One should follow that.
translations.idiomatic: That reading should be followed.

sentences.zh: 然高祖時蓋兼領軍，南史書領軍在徐州刺史下。」

translations.literal: Yet in Gaozu's time he probably also held Defender-General; the Southern History places Defender-General below Inspector of Xu Province."
translations.idiomatic: Yet Gaozu likely held Defender-General concurrently; Southern History lists it below Inspector of Xu Province."

sentences.zh: 由是王謐等諸人時失民望 「時失民望」，北監本、殿本作「時眾民望」。

translations.literal: Hence Wang Mi and the others at the time had lost the people's expectation—"at the time had lost the people's expectation": Northern Directorate and Palace editions read "at the time the multitude's expectation."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi and others "had lost the people's expectation": Northern Directorate and Palace editions read "the multitude's expectation."

sentences.zh: 三朝本、毛本、局本作「時失民望」。

translations.literal: Three-Dynasty edition, Mao edition, and Bureau edition read "at the time had lost the people's expectation."
translations.idiomatic: Three-Dynasty, Mao, and Bureau editions read "had lost the people's expectation."

sentences.zh: 李慈銘宋書札記云：「當作時失人望」。

translations.literal: Li Ciming's Notes on the Book of Song says: "It should read at the time had lost men's expectation."
translations.idiomatic: Li Ciming argues it should read "had lost men's expectation."

sentences.zh: 今從三朝本、毛本、局本。

translations.literal: Now following the Three-Dynasty, Mao, and Bureau editions.
translations.idiomatic: The Three-Dynasty, Mao, and Bureau reading is followed here.

sentences.zh: 光祿勳卞承之 「卞承之」各本並作「丁承之」。

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Household Bian Chengzhi—"Bian Chengzhi" appears as "Ding Chengzhi" in every edition.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Imperial Household Bian Chengzhi: every edition reads Ding Chengzhi.

sentences.zh: 據晉書桓玄傳改。

translations.literal: Changed per Jin History, biography of Huan Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Changed per Jin History, Huan Xuan's biography.

sentences.zh: 按通鑑晉安帝義熙三年殺殷仲文時，並誅卞承之，蓋即其人。

translations.literal: According to Comprehensive Mirror, when Yin Zhongwen was executed in the third year of Yixi under Emperor An of Jin, Bian Chengzhi was executed together with him—probably this is the man.
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror, Yixi 3, executes Bian Chengzhi with Yin Zhongwen—likely the same man.

sentences.zh: 桓玄兄子歆 「兄子歆」各本並作「兒子韶」。

translations.literal: Huan Xuan's elder brother's son Xin—"elder brother's son Xin" appears as "son Shao" in every edition.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Xuan's elder brother's son Xin: every edition reads "son Shao."

sentences.zh: 據通鑑晉安帝元興三年改。

translations.literal: Changed per Comprehensive Mirror, third year of Yuanxing under Emperor An of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Changed per Comprehensive Mirror, Yuanxing 3.

sentences.zh: 道規破玄大將郭銓等于桑落洲 「郭銓」各本作「鄭鈐」，舊本臨川王道規傳

translations.literal: Daogui broke Huan Xuan's great general Guo Quan and others at Sangluo Isle—"Guo Quan" appears as "Zheng Ling" in every edition; old edition, biography of Linchuan Prince Daogui
translations.idiomatic: Daogui defeated Guo Quan at Sangluo Isle: every edition reads Zheng Ling; the old Linchuan Prince Daogui biography

sentences.zh: (新本已改正)

translations.literal: (the new edition has already corrected this)
translations.idiomatic: (corrected in the new edition)

sentences.zh: 及御覽一二八引徐爰宋書作「郭鈐」，本書劉懷肅傳及晉書桓玄傳、通鑑作「郭銓」。

translations.literal: and Imperial Readings 128 citing Xu Ai's Book of Song read "Guo Ling"; this book's biography of Liu Huaisu and Jin History, Huan Xuan's biography, and Comprehensive Mirror read "Guo Quan."
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Readings 128 has Guo Ling; this book's Liu Huaisu biography, Jin History, and Comprehensive Mirror have Guo Quan.

sentences.zh: 按作「郭銓」是，今改正。

translations.literal: According to this, reading Guo Quan is correct; now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Quan is correct and is adopted here.

sentences.zh: 眾軍下擊大破之 「眾軍」各本並作「眾驚」，據元龜一八四改。

translations.literal: The mass army descended and struck, breaking them greatly—"mass army" appears as "mass alarm" in every edition; changed per Essentials of the Yuan Dynasty 184.
translations.idiomatic: The mass army descended and broke them: every edition reads "mass alarm"; changed per Yuan Dynasty Essentials 184.

sentences.zh: 璩弟子脩之時為玄屯騎校尉 「脩之」各本並譌「循之」，據南史及通鑑改。

translations.literal: Qu's nephew Xiuzhi at the time was Xuan's Colonel of Resolute Cavalry—"Xiuzhi" is corrupted as "Xunzhi" in every edition; changed per History of the Southern Dynasties and Comprehensive Mirror.
translations.idiomatic: Qu's nephew Xiuzhi, then Xuan's Colonel of Resolute Cavalry: every edition corrupts the name to Xunzhi; changed per Southern History and Comprehensive Mirror.

sentences.zh: 玄從子振逃於華容之涌中 「涌中」各本作「浦中」，據南史及晉書桓彝傳曾孫振附傳改。

translations.literal: Xuan's cousin Zhen fled into the Yong of Huarong—"in the Yong" appears as "in the Pu" in every edition; changed per History of the Southern Dynasties and Jin History, appended biography of Zhen, great-grandson of Huan Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's cousin Zhen fled into the Yong of Huarong: every edition reads Pu; changed per Southern History and Jin History, Zhen's appended biography.

sentences.zh: 按杜預左傳莊十八年注：「涌水在南郡華容縣。

translations.literal: According to Du Yu's commentary on the Zuo Tradition, eighteenth year of Duke Zhuang: "The Yong River is in Huarong County, Nan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yu on Zuo Tradition, Duke Zhuang 18: "The Yong River is in Huarong County, Nan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 」水經江水注：「江水又東，涌水注之。

translations.literal: " Commentary on the Water Classic, Jiang section: "The Jiang again flows east, and the Yong River flows into it.
translations.idiomatic: Water Classic, Jiang section: "The Jiang flows east and the Yong enters it.

sentences.zh: 水自夏水南通於江，謂之涌口。」

translations.literal: The water comes south from Xia River into the Jiang—this is called Yong Mouth."
translations.idiomatic: It joins the Jiang from Xia River south—called Yong Mouth."

sentences.zh: 輒申攝眾軍先上 「申」字三朝本空白，各本作「輒攝眾軍」，不空白。

translations.literal: Then declared assumption of command over the mass army and advanced first—character "declare" is blank in the Three-Dynasty edition; every edition reads "then assumed command over the mass army" without a blank.
translations.idiomatic: Then declared assumption of command over the mass army: the Three-Dynasty edition leaves "declare" blank; other editions omit it.

sentences.zh: 今據元龜一八四補。

translations.literal: Now supplemented per Essentials of the Yuan Dynasty 184.
translations.idiomatic: Declare is restored per Yuan Dynasty Essentials 184.

sentences.zh: 制路日直植城 句有譌。

translations.literal: Control the road, day by day plant cities—the sentence is corrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Control the road, day by day plant cities: the sentence is corrupt.

sentences.zh: 鮮卑貪 南史作「鮮卑性貪」。

translations.literal: The Xianbei are greedy—History of the Southern Dynasties reads "the Xianbei by nature are greedy."
translations.idiomatic: The Xianbei are greedy: Southern History reads "by nature are greedy."

sentences.zh: 通鑑作「鮮卑貪婪」。

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror reads "the Xianbei are greedy and rapacious."
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror reads "greedy and rapacious."

sentences.zh: 乃升綱於樓車 「樓車」各本並作「樓上」，據通鑑改。

translations.literal: Then raised Gang on the tower cart—"tower cart" appears as "on the tower" in every edition; changed per Comprehensive Mirror.
translations.idiomatic: Raised Gang on the tower cart: every edition reads "on the tower"; changed per Comprehensive Mirror.

sentences.zh: 十月自河北歸順 各本並無「自」字。

translations.literal: Tenth month, came from north of the He and submitted—every edition lacks the character "from."
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month, came from north of the He and submitted: every edition lacks from.

sentences.zh: 通鑑晉義熙五年作「段宏自魏奔於裕」。

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror, fifth year of Yixi under Jin, reads "Duan Hong fled from Wei to Yu."
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror, Yixi 5: "Duan Hong fled from Wei to Yu."

sentences.zh: 孫虨宋書考論云：「河北上當有自字」。

translations.literal: Sun Ban's Collation of the Book of Song says: "Above north of the He there should be the character from."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ban: "from should stand before north of the He."

sentences.zh: 按孫說是，今補。

translations.literal: According to Sun's statement it is so; now supplemented.
translations.idiomatic: Sun is correct; from is added.

sentences.zh: 殺其王公以下 「王公」各本作「亡命」，據南史、元龜一八四、通鑑晉安帝義熙六年改。

translations.literal: Killed those from princes and ministers downward—"princes and ministers" appears as "fugitives" in every edition; changed per History of the Southern Dynasties, Essentials of the Yuan Dynasty 184, and Comprehensive Mirror, sixth year of Yixi under Emperor An of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Killed those from princes and ministers downward: every edition reads fugitives; changed per Southern History, Yuan Essentials 184, and Comprehensive Mirror, Yixi 6.

sentences.zh: 今方頓兵堅城之下 「頓」各本並作「領」，據建康實錄、通鑑晉安帝義熙六年改。

translations.literal: Now halted the army beneath a strong city—"halt" appears as "lead" in every edition; changed per Records of Jiankang and Comprehensive Mirror, sixth year of Yixi under Emperor An of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Now halted the army beneath a strong city: every edition reads lead; changed per Records of Jiankang and Comprehensive Mirror, Yixi 6.

sentences.zh: 廣武將軍劉懷默屯建陽門外 「劉懷默」各本並作「劉默」，據晉書安帝紀、建康實錄補。

translations.literal: General of Expansive Might Liu Huaimo garrisoned outside the Jianyang Gate—"Liu Huaimo" appears as "Liu Mo" in every edition; supplemented per Jin History, Annals of Emperor An, and Records of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huaimo garrisoned outside the Jianyang Gate: every edition reads Liu Mo; restored per Jin Annals of Emperor An and Records of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 懷默見劉懷慎傳。

translations.literal: Huaimo is treated in the biography of Liu Huaishen.
translations.idiomatic: Huaimo appears in Liu Huaishen's biography.

sentences.zh: 命參軍褚叔度朱齡石率勁勇千餘人過淮 「褚叔度」各本並譌「諸葛叔度」。

translations.literal: Ordered Staff Officer Chu Shudu and Zhu Lingshi to lead more than a thousand picked men across the Huai—"Chu Shudu" is corrupted as "Zhuge Shudu" in every edition.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered Chu Shudu and Zhu Lingshi across the Huai: every edition corrupts Chu to Zhuge.

sentences.zh: 據通典兵典改。

translations.literal: Changed per Comprehensive Institutions, Military Canon.
translations.idiomatic: Changed per Comprehensive Institutions, Military Canon.

sentences.zh: 又見本書褚叔度傳，時為中軍諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Also seen in this book's biography of Chu Shudu; at the time he was Middle Army Adviser.
translations.idiomatic: This book's Chu Shudu biography confirms it; he was then Middle Army Adviser.

sentences.zh: 盧循遣其大將荀林寇江陵 臨川王道規傳作「荀林」。

translations.literal: Lu Xun sent his great general Xun Lin to raid Jiangling—the biography of Linchuan Prince Daogui reads "Xun Lin."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun sent Xun Lin against Jiangling: Linchuan Prince Daogui's biography reads Xun Lin.

sentences.zh: 晉書姚興載記及通鑑作「苟林」。

translations.literal: Jin History, Annals of Yao Xing, and Comprehensive Mirror read "Gou Lin."
translations.idiomatic: Jin History, Yao Xing's annals, and Comprehensive Mirror read Gou Lin.

sentences.zh: 今本書一律作「荀林」。

translations.literal: This book uniformly reads "Xun Lin."
translations.idiomatic: This book uniformly uses Xun Lin.

sentences.zh: 岸上軍先備火具 各本並奪「岸」字，據南史、通典兵典、通鑑晉安帝義熙六年補。

translations.literal: The troops on the bank had prepared fire equipment beforehand—every edition omits the character "bank"; supplemented per History of the Southern Dynasties, Comprehensive Institutions Military Canon, and Comprehensive Mirror, sixth year of Yixi under Emperor An of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The troops on the bank had prepared fire equipment: every edition drops bank; restored per Southern History, Military Canon, and Comprehensive Mirror, Yixi 6.
